### 4.6 Using Flutter-made Form Studio forms from Odoo (W10)

Forms are created only in Flutter (decided). Odoo already hid New, Duplicate and Import on forms, and already ran the whole assessment lifecycle - assign, launch and invite, monitor, score, release, export - on the assessment a form creates. What stopped an admin:

| # | Change | Days |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Send to Candidates** (now "Publish") stays available after the first publish, like Flutter's Publish: each press makes a new draft assessment from the form's current content; earlier assessments untouched | 0.5 |
| 2 | Publish warnings shown, as Flutter does (before, an image that failed to download was silently missing from the question candidates see) | 0.25 |
| 3 | Archiving an assessment refused while a candidate is mid-exam, as the API already does (Odoo skipped that check) | 0.25 |
| 4 | Editing forms in Odoo - see below | 0.1 |
| | **Total** | **~1-1.5** |

**Forms are read-only in Odoo (decided).** Flutter saves its whole copy of an open form every 0.9 s, so an Odoo edit would be silently overwritten; edits happen in Flutter. Round 1: prod published form 46 has 5 editable inputs plus Save; ours has 0 (B4-18). Prod has 25 forms, 16 published, 23 "Form:" generators, 2 with an "(n)" suffix, so re-publishing already happens on prod (F2-20).

### 4.7 Order of work and schema footprint

Order agreed 2026-09-22 (both plans): (1) login fix and the scoring collision fix - both hurting prod; (2) regression and scale fixes and the settings; (3) individual scoring (depends on 1); (4) retire "Same questions" with the count lock, Scored / Score Pending chips; (5) imports; (6) Form Studio forms from Odoo; (7) Question Templates on the generator; (8) grading: text-only, group caches, model readiness, then calibration on the prod copy before the push. Every step: full suites on an upgraded local copy (never prod, never stage) and a browser pass. The model catalog is code, not data.

- Plan footprint: "three new nullable columns (`score_outlier_checked_at`, `rescore_request_key`, the golden file name on generators), one new table (caches) and one system parameter (the deploy time)". Superseded 2026-09-23 (B6-02): 7 columns on 4 tables and 2 tables - full list in Part 1 §1.3. System parameters added: `assessments_be_v2.score_outlier_checks_since` (set by the first cron run), `assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache` (engineer switch, absent = off; superseded 2026-09-23 by Q3: absent = `groups`), `assessments_be_v2.verdict_requires_current_prompt` (absent = on), `assessments_be_v2.scoring_parallel_calls` (setting, absent = 4). Final counts from the code (2026-09-24): 7 new columns on business tables plus 10 on transient tables, 2 new tables, 3 dropped transient columns (Part 0 §0.5 L4); switch table: Part 0 §0.5 J. Q20 (2026-09-24) adds 1 business column (`assessments_be.pass_threshold`, NULL on every existing row), 1 transient column (`res_config_settings.assessments_be_default_pass_threshold`) and 1 system parameter (`assessments_be_v2.default_pass_threshold`, unset = 70): **8 business + 11 transient columns** in all, checked in `information_schema` after `-u`.
- Risk noted 2026-09-22: all work uncommitted for ~5 weeks; daily patch backups outside the repos (W0). The prod copy for calibration is needed when the grading work (item 8) starts, about 3 weeks in. Superseded 2026-09-23 (Q2): no prod copy; the check ran on made-up answers (Part 5 §5.6.10).

### 4.8 Settings parity (wave 2, 2026-09-18) - partly superseded by W7

Shipped in 19.0.3.22.0 (on prod).
- Three Odoo form settings match the Flutter console in name, group, order and help text. A new **Scoring** group held, in Flutter's order, *Same questions for everybody*, *Shuffle Questions* and *Grade subjective answers automatically*. The group that used to hold the last of those was renamed **Violations** (it holds the violation action and the cap).
- `preserve_question_order` is the logical **inverse** of Flutter's *Shuffle Questions* and was deliberately NOT relabelled: a checkbox reading "Shuffle Questions" that ticks to mean "do not shuffle" would be worse. The form gets a computed, **non-stored** mirror, `shuffle_questions`, with an inverse setter (`assessment.py::_compute_shuffle_questions` / `_inverse_shuffle_questions`). No new column; the stored negative stays the single source of truth that `action_start`, the late-add provisioner and Form Studio's publish branch on.
- `same_questions_for_all`'s default flipped `False` -> `True` to match the Flutter create screen. A Python `default=` applies only when a create omits the field, so no existing assessment moved; every bare create from then on (Odoo's New button, an API create without the key) drew one shared paper. **Superseded 2026-09-22 by W7:** the flag is retired entirely; every paper draws one shared set and the switch is gone from both UIs.
- Flutter live bug fixed in the same pass: `_ConfigTab._ro` was a capability check with no state in it, so all three switches were editable in every state while the server refused two (`same_questions_for_all` is not in `POST_DRAFT_FIELDS`; `shuffle_questions` is folded into `preserve_question_order` by `_apply_shuffle_alias` BEFORE the draft gate). Toggling either on a running assessment moved a switch on screen and came back a silent 409. The two draw settings then locked once the assessment left draft; automatic grading locks only on done/cancelled, matching the Odoo form. A Notice under the autograde switch - only past draft and only when on - says it queues everyone still to submit and NOBODY who already has, and names **Re-score This Assessment** (`action_llm_score_all`) as the retro-fill.

### 4.9 Live question-generation stats (plan, 2026-09-29) - awaiting approval

**Ask (owner, 2026-09-29 prod e2e test):** show question-generation stats in real time on the generator screen, the way the Assessment page shows scoring stats. Nothing is built yet; decisions in (g).

**(a) What we mirror - scoring on the Assessment page (read from code, not run).**
- UI: `ethara-assessment-fe/lib/assessment/screens/admin/assessment_detail_screen.dart` - blue "Scoring." notice with spinner and the server's one-line summary (`N queued · N scoring · N scored · N failed · N stopped`, 682-696); red "Grading is not running." notice with the drainer's reason (629-666); "Scored X/Y" notice (616-628); Score All / Score Failed Candidates (n) / Kill buttons (885-1010). Text notices only - no bar, no cost, no ETA.
- Refresh: screen-local one-shot `Timer` `_tickScoring` (319-355): 5 s, backing off to 15 s then 30 s while nothing changes, 1 min while stalled, stops after 720 ticks, pauses when the tab is hidden, one full reload 0-5 s after the run ends.
- API: `GET /api/v1/scoring?assessment_id=` (`controllers/api/admin.py:1776-1883`) - `lanes`, `queued`, `phase`, `summary`, `drainer{stalled,crons_*,reason}`, `errored[]`; phase/summary from ONE `_read_group` in `_compute_scoring_progress` (`models/assessment.py:1416-1566`).

**(b) What generation has today.**
- Generator screen (`generator_detail_screen.dart`) loads on init/route change only; the "Generation state" pill (2697-2726) shows `sop_gen_state` and, after the run, `sop_gen_report` or "N generated, M approved". A `JobCard` "Pipelines" panel exists but renders only in demo mode (2930-2960).
- Live refresh is the store-wide `pollGeneration` (`app_store.dart:7896-8001`): every 2 s, capped at 90 ticks (~3 min), and each tick re-reads EVERY page of `/generators` and `/drafts`. A run can sit `queued` up to 5 min (the SOP cron runs every 5 min and Generate does not trigger it), so the poll often gives up before the run starts.
- Server state: `sop_gen_state` idle/queued/generating/finalizing/done/failed/cancelled (`prompt.py:193-234`); drafts carry `image_state`, `video_state`, `image_render_attempts`; the LLM ledger (`assessments.be.llm.usage`, `prompt_id` indexed, committed on a side cursor so visible mid-run) records every call with operation, cost and a step note.
- Gaps: no run start/finish timestamps (no elapsed time, no ETA); drafts are created in one transaction at the end, so the draft count is 0 for the whole authoring phase; no generator-level summary endpoint; the Flutter `Generator` model ignores `draft_counts`; `/api/v1/ledger` needs `require_operator`.

**(c) What the owner saw on prod that this should explain (2026-09-29).** 16 drafts at 11:48:27; image drafts showed "Pending" / "No image yet" for up to 12 min because the image cron renders 2 drafts every 5 min (`prompt.py:4281`, `data/cron.xml:145`); draft 85 went to `failed` with no retry in the app (only `retry_video` exists); the Drafts list did not reflect renders that had already committed.

**(d) Proposed stats (option A, recommended).** One banner on the generator page, same look and wording style as scoring, plus a small stats block on the Generation tab:
- Queued: "Queued - starts at the next generation slot (~HH:MM)".
- Authoring: "Writing questions · step <main / retry / top-up / critique / answer keys> · N model calls · $X · M min elapsed" (step and cost from ledger rows for this generator since the run started).
- Media: "Rendering media · images R/T (F failed) · videos R/T · next image batch ~HH:MM (2 every 5 min)".
- Ready: "16 drafts ready for review · P pending · A approved · D denied · run cost $X · took M min".
- Red "Generation is not running" notice when stalled (queued past its slot, image/Veo cron inactive or overdue), with the reason, like the drainer notice.
- Buttons in the scoring pattern: **Retry failed images (n)** (new) next to the existing Kill Generation.

**(e) Build.**
- Backend: `GET /api/v1/generators/<id>/progress` (`require_staff`) returning `phase`, `summary`, `lanes{drafts, images, videos}`, `run{started_at, finished_at, elapsed_s, llm_calls, cost_usd, last_step, last_step_at}`, `media{images_left, next_image_at, est_minutes}`, `drainer{stalled, reason}`, `errored[]`. One `_read_group` over drafts plus one aggregate over the ledger for this generator, the same shape as `_compute_scoring_progress`. `POST /api/v1/drafts/<id>/retry_images` and `POST /api/v1/generators/<id>/retry_failed_images` (failed -> pending; mirrors `retry_video`).
- Schema: 2 nullable columns on `assessments_be_prompt` - `sop_gen_started_at`, `sop_gen_finished_at` - set by the SOP cron. Needed to scope the ledger to "this run" and show elapsed time; no backfill (NULL on old runs shows no elapsed time). Version bump at push time only.
- Frontend: a screen-local `_tickGeneration` with the scoring backoff (5 s -> 15 s -> 30 s while unchanged, stop when idle and no media pending, pause when hidden, quiet reloads only - no screen swap on a tick); retire `pollGeneration`'s 2 s full re-read of every page for this screen. Parse `draft_counts`.
- Why short polling, not a long-poll watch: a held long-poll keeps one DB connection per open screen for up to a minute, and prod Postgres sat at 192-199 of 200 connections on 2026-09-29 (the scale-up outage). The backed-off poll is cheaper on connections than the current 2 s loop.
- Tests: backend unit tests for every phase and the stalled reasons; Flutter widget tests for each banner state and the backoff (fake clock - gate timers as in `flutter-test-triage`); a browser pass on a local run.

**(f) Options.**

| Option | What | Days |
|---|---|---|
| A (recommended) | (d) + (e): scoring-style banner, progress endpoint, 2 timestamps, retry-failed-images | ~2 |
| B | A + a phase stepper (Queued -> Authoring -> Media -> Ready), per-phase durations and a cost split (text / image / video) | ~3 |
| C | Frontend only from existing data (`draft_counts`, draft image/video pills); no authoring-phase info, no elapsed time, no cost (ledger role) | ~0.5 |

**(g) Decisions needed.** (1) A, B or C. (2) Banner on the page plus the tab block, or the tab only. (3) Include Retry failed images (and a "render now" trigger that skips the 5-minute wait) in this piece. (4) Show run cost to every staff user, or operators only, as `/ledger` does today.

**Related fixes from the same test, not part of this plan:** the image cron marks a draft `failed` on `SerializationFailure` and counts it as rendered (`prompt.py:4290-4312`; root cause under investigation); `draft_task_template_from_sop` starts at `max_tokens=4000` and is cut off every time (`services/vertex.py:5437`); the draft endpoint returns 500 on a Vertex 429 (`controllers/api/task_templates.py:207`); resource upload returns 500 on NUL bytes (`prompt.py:5010`).

### 5.2 Before the deploy

> **For the 19.0.3.23.0 push, the procedure is Part 0 §0.5, the deploy note for devops (steps A-L; the switch table is in J).** §5.2-§5.5 keep the background; every step is in §0.5, and older lines that differ are marked superseded. In short: backend first, app second; one `-u` job before new pods take traffic, never in the image CMD; no `prod:` commit message; a DB snapshot before `-u`; parallel calls left at 4; a rollback that runs `-u` with the previous code and drops 17 columns.
> Superseded 2026-09-24: "`scoring_parallel_calls` = 2 before the new pods take traffic" (Q6).

**Fix first:** round-1 blockers B1-B5 (Part 1 §1.4.1). Done 2026-09-24 (Part 1 §1.4).

**Calibration gate (W15) - not met, not waived (2026-09-23).** The plan (§2.17), the calibration design (§3.13), the runbook (§5.6) and the old change summary's deploy line ("run the calibration on the prod copy first") all put it before the push. The prod copy has not been provided (Part 1 §1.4.2), so it has not run. Before the push, either the owner provides the copy and the new-request arm passes, or the owner waives it in writing; record either, with its date, in Part 1 §1.2.
- Superseded 2026-09-23 (Q2): no prod copy, ever. The gate is replaced by the paid synthetic check (Q2b, done 2026-09-24, §5.6.10) and the first-paper spot check (Part 0 §0.5 J7).

**When:** only when **no scoring run is active and no exam is live**.
- Grading switches to the new text-only request at deploy; a paper mid-run would be graded two ways. (Round 1, B6-16: every unscored graded answer on a submitted attempt today sits on an archived paper or a cancelled attempt, which the cron skips, so nothing half-graded is touched by either build.)
- The `-u` adds columns with `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`, which takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `assessments_be_response`, `assessments_be`, `assessments_be_prompt`, `assessments_be_llm_usage` - blocking reads and writes - until the module commits (after all data files load). The new partial index is a plain `CREATE INDEX` (not CONCURRENTLY) with 0 entries: tens of ms on prod's 31,959 answers. Short, but plan for it (B6-03). G5-13 later measured locks on 6 assessment tables for about 1-5 s (Part 0 §0.5 I2).
- Check at deploy time (B6-12): count of evaluators with `state = in_progress`, or `llm_state = scoring`, or `scoring_requested` with `llm_state in (pending, partial)` = 0; `/api/v1/scoring` `lanes.scoring = 0`. On 2026-09-23 ~11:30 UTC prod had 0 in progress, 0 scoring, nothing queued.
- `tools/deploy_gate.py` checks live exams but reads `meta.hasMore` while the API sends `has_more`, so it stops after 200 of 8,210 attempts, and it does not check scoring runs (B6-13): fix it or do the check above by hand. Superseded 2026-09-24: fixed (S14) - it pages through every attempt and exits 1 while `lanes.scoring > 0`. **`ETP_LOGIN` must be an assessments Admin** (`group_assessment_manager`): `/api/v1/scoring` is Admin-only, so a Manager login gets 403 there and the gate exits 2 on every deploy (Part 0 §0.5 H3). It only sees live (non-archived) assessments by design - a stranded sitting on a closed paper cannot be interrupted by a deploy and would otherwise block every future one.
- `tools/check_settings_in_range.py` is the pre-deploy settings gate; it reads `constants.SETTING_RANGES`.

**Order:** **backend first (`-u`), app second** (B3 blocker). Our app on today's backend breaks chips, Emails, per-answer re-score and shows old verdicts (F1-07, F3-10, F4-18..20). The deployed app is fine on the new backend: every changed key is additive (F4-06..09, F4-12..17). After the app deploy, tell admins to reload open tabs - the bundle has no service worker and is `no-cache`, so only tabs open before the deploy keep the old build (F4-01).

**Database connections:** lanes size themselves to Odoo's `db_maxconn` (per process), counting each lane's own 2 connections plus 2 per call. Pool 64 -> **3 calls per lane** (setting stays 4; Settings shows the value in use); 4 needs `db_maxconn` >= 80. Confirm prod Postgres `max_connections` has room for ~+20 grading connections across all pods. Read `workers`, `db_maxconn`, `max_cron_threads`, `db_replica_host` from the prod odoo.conf / pod env (prefork changes the arithmetic - §3.4). Superseded 2026-09-23 (Q6, owner's Grafana read): prod `db_maxconn` is 600, so every lane runs all 4 calls; `max_connections` is 200; a bulk run adds about 16 connections; a refused connection now waits for the next tick.

**Old verdicts gate (decided 2026-09-23 - leave ON).** Candidates now see the grader's prose verdict (`score_verdict`) on released answers. Verdicts written under the old instructions were meant for admins, so the gate is built and on by default (audit apc-3 / swe-flutter-4):

| System parameter | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `assessments_be_v2.verdict_requires_current_prompt` | on (absent = on) | `1`/absent: `score_verdict` is sent only when the answer's `llm_prompt_version` equals the fingerprint of the instructions in force; an older or unversioned verdict is sent as the empty string (the key is never dropped, so older Flutter builds keep working and show no verdict). `0`/`false`/`no`/`off`: every verdict is sent, as before the gate. Changes take effect with no deploy. |

- **Do not set it to `0` as a deploy step.** All 1,411 released verdicts on prod carry the OLD fingerprint `bundled:34c42d2f` (2,735 verdicts overall), so the gate hides every one - correct, because **no deployed client has ever rendered them**: the live bundle (`assessment.ethara.ai/main.dart.js`, built 2026-09-21 03:35, FE `48e8434`) has zero references to `score_verdict` / `scoreVerdict`. Rendering the prose verdict is NEW in this wave (`models.dart`, `exam_screen.dart`: 0 occurrences at FE HEAD, 3 each in the working tree; `score_verdict` appears nowhere in the app's committed history). Setting `0` would not restore anything; it would expose 1,411 verdicts written under admin-only instructions for the first time. Turning it off is a product decision about the historical corpus, taken deliberately, never during a deploy.
- What candidates see today under the word "verdict" is the long-standing `verdict` label (Correct / Incorrect / Partly correct / Passed / Failed / No Grade) plus `feedback`, credit and deduction reasons, under the heading "THE JUDGE'S VERDICT". Two different payload keys; only the label ships today.
- Superseded 2026-09-23: "nothing is leaking in production" - deduction/credit reasons with admin-voice text are drawn today and point values sit in the JSON (C8, C9, F3-07); the gate covers only the prose verdict. Superseded: the change summary's "set it to `0` after the precheck scan comes back clean" (F3-12).
- With the gate on, this push changes nothing for the 1,411 released answers and shows a prose verdict only on answers graded after the push. Re-run the verdict scan (§5.6.2) before any future push that edits `prompts/scoring.md`.
- The gate is backend-only (F3-10) - another reason for backend first. Code comment "an older Flutter build reads score_verdict" (`serializers.py:1093`) is false (C26).

**Expected new fingerprint:** `bundled:785826a5` = `sha256(prompts/scoring.md.strip())[:8]` of the working tree. The staged copy is still `bundled:f8a15cce`, so stage the working tree first (Part 0 §0.5 D). Re-derive it as the last step before the push; any edit to `prompts/scoring.md` changes it. Superseded 2026-09-24: `bundled:3702673a` (then `bundled:f8a15cce`, then `bundled:11b900fb`).

**Also in the same push:** `custom_addons/api_auth_gateway/controllers/main.py` (Python only; the gateway stays at 19.0.1.0.0 and needs no `-u` - B6-10). Nothing outside the module and the gateway is changed (B6-09).

- Then deploy the app build. The full order, the `prod:` rule, the snapshot and the checks: Part 0 §0.5 F-K.

### 5.4 After the deploy

Shards 4, batch 20, attempts 3 are already set on prod (F2-13). Groups under the model's minimum are left out, so prod's papers batch as before (§3.10). Set it to `off` only to rule the cache out while chasing a grading problem; flip only when no bulk run is going. Hold its release for owner review (Q16). Superseded 2026-09-24: "until calibration passes" - there is no prod-copy calibration (Q2).

### 5.5 Rollback

> The rollback procedure is Part 0 §0.5 L, with the exact list of what the rollback `-u` drops (L4). The lines below are background.

- **Cache switch:** set `assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache` to `off` - one step, no deploy (the cache is ON by default since Q3).
- **Verdict gate:** already the safe value (on).
- **Everything else:** roll the app back first, then the backend, together (F1-07, F3-10). Redeploy the previous backend build **and run `-u assessments_be_v2` on it** - without `-u`, HEAD code on an upgraded DB fails in `res.config.settings` (`UndefinedColumn: column "assessments_be_scoring_prompt" ... does not exist`) (B6-15).
- **Clear queued re-score requests** - otherwise the new build grades them (and spends) the moment it is redeployed: the keyed lane query has no `scoring_requested` filter and keys are cleared only by Kill or by grading (apc-9, B6-17):

```sql
UPDATE assessments_be_response SET rescore_request_key = NULL WHERE rescore_request_key IS NOT NULL;
```

- Superseded 2026-09-24: the SQL is not needed. The rollback `-u` drops `rescore_request_key` with the queued keys in it (Part 0 §0.5 L4); the SQL would matter only if the code were rolled back without `-u`, which §0.5 forbids.

- **`-u` with the previous code drops 17 columns** (G5-11): `llm_usage.cached_tokens`, `response.rescore_request_key`, `scoring_last_*`, `score_outlier_checked_at`, `upload_golden_filename`, plus transient columns. Export `cached_tokens` and `scoring_last_*` first if they matter. Orphan tables are harmless. Itemised from the final code in Part 0 §0.5 L4: 7 business and 10 transient columns; the 2 new tables stay, orphaned. Caches expire within 15 minutes. Outlier flags catch up as papers are scored again. Superseded 2026-09-23: "the new columns and tables stay in place, unused".
- Superseded 2026-09-23: "redeploy the previous build; queued re-score requests are ignored (click again after re-deploy)".

### 5.6 Calibration runbook (W15)

Before the push: prove that the new grading request (text only, trimmed) moves marks no more than the model's own run-to-run wobble. Tools: `tools/calibration/`. Design: Part 3 §3.13.

> Superseded 2026-09-23 (Q2): there is no prod copy, ever. The runbook now runs in **synthetic mode** (§5.6.0a): real prod questions, made-up answers, a pure-HEAD baseline. The prod-copy steps below stay for a future copy. The 2026-09-24 runs are recorded in §5.6.10.

**Nothing is written to prod, to stage, or to the copy.** Every tool opens its own database cursor and rolls it back. A grade is stored only inside a savepoint that is rolled back once the result has been read. Ledger rows are kept in memory. Results go to JSONL files on disk: answer ids, scores and counts only, never answer text.

Round-1 notes before you start: prod has only 2 image_prompt, 2 video_prompt and <=7 LLM-graded image_ab answers, so add seeded answers or grade paper 3's pending answers on the copy for those types (the harness would need to accept them) (B3-23); prod has no fallback, so the fallback arm tests nothing prod runs - drop or re-scope it (B1-09); no prod paper forms a cache group, so calibrate the cached arm on a paper shaped like evals-* (B3-15). Handled 2026-09-24: synthetic mode seeds every type, the fallback arm was dropped, and the 13-question synthetic paper forms a cache group.

#### 5.6.0 What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| Prod backup | `pg_dump -Fc` of the prod database **plus its filestore** (tarball), from the owner |
| Two checkouts | **new** = the push candidate (all W-items); **baseline** = exactly what prod runs today (prompt `bundled:34c42d2f`): a `git archive` of HEAD, nothing else (R6-01) |
| Assessments | 1-2 finished ones, ~1,000 graded answers, every question type used, including image labelling |
| Vertex | a service account the owner agrees can pay for ~$30-70 |
| Python | the venv of either checkout (`.venv/bin/python`), Postgres 16 |

All commands run from a checkout root. `PY=.venv/bin/python`, `T=custom_addons/assessments_be_v2/tools/calibration`, and `calib/` is a work folder outside both repos. Each script takes `-c <odoo conf> -d <database>` and `--odoo-src src` (the default).

#### 5.6.0a Synthetic mode (Q2b; used 2026-09-24)

No prod copy (Q2). Instead: real prod **question** content, made-up **answers**, and no candidate data anywhere.

1. **Export the questions**, read-only, from prod: `assessments.be.question` with its images, videos, dimensions and options, plus the images prod stores as binaries. The 2026-09-24 runs used 13 questions: subjective 122, 810, 764, 355; image_label 135, 120; image_prompt 809, 948; video_prompt 190, 191, 791; image_ab 30, 59 (every image_ab with official reasoning). Prod stores clips as URLs only, so both sides grade video questions without the clip, as prod does (`--allow-missing-media` on the baseline).
2. **Write the made-up answers.** The runs used 22 personas x 5 types = 110; the kinds cycle correct, partial, wrong, off-topic, a note to the grader, near-blank.
3. **Build the synthetic database** on a copy made for it, with crons and mail servers off:
   ```bash
   createdb -T <scratch copy> <synth db>
   $PY $T/synthetic.py -c <conf> -d <synth db> --questions prod_questions.json --answers answers.json
   ```
   It **writes and commits**. It first deletes every attempt and answer not on a paper an earlier build made (a copy keeps its source's candidates, FU14). Then it adds a generator per prod form, the questions, one paper, one blanked candidate per persona with their answers (never graded), prod's grading settings (batch 20, no fallback, `scoring_cache` = `groups`), and lists the paper in the system parameter **`calibration.synthetic_papers`**. It refuses a database with an active cron or mail server. It keeps the copy's `hr.applicant` rows (never sent anywhere); drop the database afterwards.
4. **The marker is scoped.** The arms skip the live and unblanked checks only when every answer id, trick hosts included, sits on a listed paper. A database marked synthetic that still holds any other answer is refused (FU14). Anything else gets the full checks (R6-09): active mail servers or crons, unblanked applicant emails, roster emails and candidate logins.
5. **Baseline = pure HEAD:** `git -C <backend repo> archive <HEAD sha> src custom_addons | tar -x -C <baseline dir>`, with a conf whose `addons_path` points into that folder. The runs used HEAD `0d09cdfb5` (prompt `bundled:34c42d2f`). Pin the sha: HEAD moves after the push. The baseline arm drives HEAD's single grading entry point, `_score_submission`, inside a rolled-back savepoint, and refuses `--model` (R6-01).
6. **Upgrade** the synthetic database with the new code (`-u assessments_be_v2 --stop-after-init`), then load a Vertex service account in Settings. The paid runs used a non-prod Vertex project. Blank the keys again afterwards.
7. **Dry-run, then run** as in §5.6.5-§5.6.7, with an ids file covering the synthetic paper's answers and `--max-usd` set to the approved budget. Run the new arms from the new checkout and the baseline from the baseline folder, on the same database.

#### 5.6.1 Restore the copy, blank candidates FIRST

The owner should run the blanking on a staging restore, so names and emails never leave prod. If the dump arrives unblanked, run it before anything else touches the database.

```bash
createdb calib_base
pg_restore --no-owner --no-acl -d calib_base prod.dump
psql -d calib_base -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
BEGIN;
-- Nothing on the copy may send mail, fetch mail, or run a cron (grading crons call Vertex).
UPDATE ir_cron SET active = false;
UPDATE ir_mail_server SET active = false;
UPDATE fetchmail_server SET active = false;
-- Candidate accounts: login = the applicant's address, or the candidate
-- group. Found BEFORE the addresses are blanked.
CREATE TEMP TABLE calib_candidate_users AS
SELECT id, partner_id FROM res_users
 WHERE id > 2 AND (lower(login) IN (SELECT lower(email_from) FROM hr_applicant
                                    WHERE email_from IS NOT NULL)
    OR id IN (SELECT r.uid FROM res_groups_users_rel r
                JOIN ir_model_data d ON d.model = 'res.groups' AND d.res_id = r.gid
               WHERE d.module = 'assessments_be_v2'
                 AND d.name = 'group_assessment_candidate'));
UPDATE res_users SET login = 'candidate-u' || id || '@blanked.invalid'
 WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM calib_candidate_users);
UPDATE res_partner SET name = 'Candidate ' || id,
       email = 'candidate-p' || id || '@blanked.invalid',
       email_normalized = 'candidate-p' || id || '@blanked.invalid',
       phone = NULL, phone_sanitized = NULL
 WHERE id IN (SELECT partner_id FROM calib_candidate_users)
    OR id IN (SELECT partner_id FROM hr_applicant WHERE partner_id IS NOT NULL);
-- Applicants.
UPDATE hr_applicant SET partner_name = 'Candidate ' || id,
       email_from = 'candidate-' || id || '@blanked.invalid',
       email_normalized = 'candidate-' || id || '@blanked.invalid',
       email_cc = NULL, partner_phone = NULL, partner_phone_sanitized = NULL;
-- Objects prod's schema does not have (B3-23): blanked only where they exist.
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
              WHERE table_name = 'hr_applicant'
                AND column_name = 'emergency_contact_phone') THEN
    UPDATE hr_applicant SET emergency_contact_phone = NULL;
  END IF;
  IF to_regclass('hr_applicant_reference') IS NOT NULL THEN
    UPDATE hr_applicant_reference SET email = NULL, phone = NULL;
  END IF;
END $$;
-- The copies the roster keeps for sorting and search.
UPDATE assessments_be_evaluator e SET candidate_name = a.partner_name,
       candidate_email = a.email_from
  FROM hr_applicant a WHERE a.id = e.applicant_id;
-- Mail that names or addresses them.
UPDATE mail_message SET email_from = NULL, body = NULL
 WHERE model IN ('hr.applicant', 'assessments.be.evaluator',
                 'assessments.be.response', 'res.partner');
UPDATE mail_mail SET email_to = NULL, email_cc = NULL, body_html = NULL;
-- Prod's S3 key is not needed: grading reads media from the database/filestore.
UPDATE ir_config_parameter SET value = ''
 WHERE key = 'assessments_be_v2.s3_secret_key';
COMMIT;
-- Must print 0 0 0.
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM hr_applicant
         WHERE email_from NOT LIKE '%@blanked.invalid'),
       (SELECT count(*) FROM assessments_be_evaluator
         WHERE candidate_email NOT LIKE '%@blanked.invalid'),
       (SELECT count(*) FROM res_users u JOIN res_groups_users_rel r ON r.uid = u.id
          JOIN ir_model_data d ON d.model = 'res.groups' AND d.res_id = r.gid
         WHERE d.module = 'assessments_be_v2'
           AND d.name = 'group_assessment_candidate'
           AND u.login NOT LIKE '%@blanked.invalid');
SQL
```

- A column that does not exist on prod's schema fails the whole transaction. **On prod's schema (B3-23): `hr_applicant.emergency_contact_phone` and the table `hr_applicant_reference` do not exist**, so the script blanks them only where they exist (the `DO` block) and runs as is on both shapes. Checked with `ON_ERROR_STOP=1` on throwaway copies: it prints 0 0 0 with both objects present and with both dropped. Superseded 2026-09-24: "remove `emergency_contact_phone = NULL` and the `hr_applicant_reference` statement before running".
- Answer text is kept, because it is what gets graded. A candidate who typed their own name into an answer is still in it.
- **Filestore.** Unpack prod's filestore to `~/Library/Application Support/Odoo/filestore/calib_base` (on Linux, `~/.local/share/Odoo/filestore/calib_base`). Today's code attaches images and clips read from it. Without it the baseline arm would grade blind, which prod did not do. The baseline runner refuses to run in that case (step 5).
- **Two databases.** The baseline runs on prod's own schema. The new code needs its additive columns:

```bash
createdb -T calib_base calib_new
cp -R ".../filestore/calib_base" ".../filestore/calib_new"
cd <new checkout> && $PY src/odoo-bin -c <conf> -d calib_new -u assessments_be_v2 --stop-after-init
```

  The upgrade touches no existing row, so answer ids are the same in both.
- **Vertex.** The copy carries prod's encrypted service account, and it decrypts on the copy. Use it only if the owner agrees that the spend lands on prod's project. Otherwise upload the calibration account in Settings on `calib_new`, then copy the four `assessments_be_v2.vertex_*` parameters to `calib_base`.

#### 5.6.2 Precheck (new checkout, `calib_new`)

```bash
$PY $T/precheck.py -c <conf> -d calib_new --assessments 812,815
```

It prints: graded answers by prompt version; the question types present; the profile-mismatch report (W12); verdicts that name grading mechanics (profile tags, thresholds, caps, percentages).

- The verdict scan is **no longer a push blocker**: the gate (§5.2) already withholds every old or unversioned verdict. What to do with its result: **nothing listed** - still do not set the parameter to `0` (no deployed client ever rendered `score_verdict`; turning the gate off would show historical verdicts for the first time); **anything listed** - leave the parameter alone; those verdicts stay hidden until the answers are re-graded under the current instructions, which stamps the new fingerprint and makes the verdict appear on its own.
- Any version other than `bundled:34c42d2f` is marked `<- FLAG` and the script exits 1. Resolve every flag before the push: `override:...` = a stored override graded it; `bundled:b39fc051` = the built-in fallback graded it; another `bundled:` value = a different file graded it; empty or `pre-versioning` = graded before versioning. Those answers were not graded by the text the baseline arm reproduces: leave them out, or find out why first. Mismatches go to the owner, who picks which to re-score.
- Round 1 expectation: all 2,735 graded answers are `bundled:34c42d2f`; the mismatch report would list 1 answer (7184) (B3-23). Add "golden", "rubric", "the candidate", "penalty" to the mechanics regex (F3-11); its current regex flags 16 of 1,411 ("fabricat...") (F3-06).

**Scan already run against production (2026-09-23)** - provenance: first run by an audit subagent without authorisation (it was stopped), then reproduced read-only under supervision (B3-12, C10). Method: every released answer carrying a verdict was read from prod (`assessments.be.response`, read-only) and scanned for profile tags, thresholds, caps, percentages, weights, lane and model names, temperature and point arithmetic. Superseded 2026-09-23: the counts are now reproduced read-only under supervision (B3-12, C10), so they are evidence, not just a lead.

| Measured | Value |
|---|---|
| Released answers carrying a verdict | **1,411** (1,414 released written answers; 3 unversioned) |
| Distinct `llm_prompt_version` across them | **1** - `bundled:34c42d2f` on every row |
| Verdicts naming grading mechanics | reported **0**; the harness regex flags **16** ("fabricat...") (F3-06) |

- The strings that tripped a deliberately wide term filter: "rubric" (16, e.g. "according to the rubric" - which the candidate-facing `feedback` already says), "point(s)" meaning an ARGUMENT not a mark (22), one "0-point rubric criteria", two "hallucinates". No profile, threshold, cap, percentage, weight, lane, model name or temperature appeared. Plain reading on round 1 also found "golden answer" 3 and 128 verdicts written about "The candidate..." (F3-06).
- None of the 1,411 carries the current fingerprint (now `bundled:785826a5`; `bundled:3702673a` when the scan ran), so the gate hides all of them - correct (§5.2).

#### 5.6.3 Pick the answers (new checkout, `calib_new`)

```bash
$PY $T/select_answers.py -c <conf> -d calib_new --assessments 812,815 --sample 1000 --seed 7 --out calib/ids.json
$PY $T/select_answers.py -c <conf> -d calib_new --assessments 812,815 --sample 200  --seed 7 --out calib/ids_200.json
```

- Stratified by question type, at least 30 per type. Grouped by candidate, so the answers grade in few calls. Deterministic for a seed; the 200 set is a subset of the 1,000 set, so the fallback arm reuses the baseline rows. Left out: image A/B answers with no official reasoning (code marks those; the grader never sees them).

#### 5.6.4 Trick answers (new checkout, `calib_new`)

```bash
$PY $T/seed_tricks.py -c <conf> -d calib_new --assessments 812,815 --out calib/tricks.json
```

- ~20 tricks, each on a real question. It borrows a real answer to that question (the "host") and swaps in the trick text, only inside a rolled-back transaction. It drafts two kinds itself: **invented** (not contradicting the key: the key's own answer plus a made-up media detail, a potted plant) and **contradicting** (A/B swapped in the official reasoning, box labels rotated, "None of this is true: ..." on a written answer, or a required element dropped from a prompt).
- **true_unlisted** tricks come out with `"answer": null`. Open the question's media, write `base` plus one claim that is true of the media but not in the key, and save it into `answer`. On labelling, `answer` is a JSON string of `{box: label}`. A trick left null is skipped.
- Finish this before any arm runs, and give every arm the same `tricks.json`.

#### 5.6.5 Dry-run every arm (free: no Vertex call)

```bash
# new checkout
$PY $T/run_new_arm.py -c <conf> -d calib_new --arm new_uncached --ids calib/ids.json --tricks calib/tricks.json --dry-run --out calib/dry_new_uncached.jsonl
$PY $T/run_new_arm.py -c <conf> -d calib_new --arm new_cached   --ids calib/ids.json --tricks calib/tricks.json --dry-run --out calib/dry_new_cached.jsonl
$PY $T/run_new_arm.py -c <conf> -d calib_new --arm new_fallback --ids calib/ids_200.json --tricks calib/tricks.json --dry-run --out calib/dry_new_fallback.jsonl
# baseline checkout (the scripts need only this tools folder, not the new module)
cd <baseline checkout>
$PY <new checkout>/$T/run_baseline_arm.py -c <conf> -d calib_base --run 1 --ids calib/ids.json --tricks calib/tricks.json --dry-run --out calib/dry_baseline.jsonl
python3 <new checkout>/$T/compare.py calib/dry_*.jsonl --out calib/dry_report.md
```

Each run builds every request with the code's own builder, stops at the HTTP call, and prints the calls, tokens and estimated cost (4.03 characters per token, 1,120 tokens per image, 982 output tokens per answer). Check:
- The baseline shows **image parts > 0**. A warning `no readable media for question(s) ...` means the filestore is missing.
- Each run prints `grading code .../<checkout>/...` - the checkout actually grading.
- Estimated total ~ $30-70 and ~250-300 calls. Calls follow the copy's `scoring_batch_size` (20 on prod).
- On a git-HEAD baseline lane the baseline runner fails with an unfriendly `AttributeError` instead of a clean `SystemExit`; it runs fine on the real pre-build lane (`etp-lanes/be-baseline`, prompt `bundled:34c42d2f`) (apc-2, refuted as a blocker). Superseded 2026-09-24 (R6-01): the baseline runs on pure HEAD (a `git archive` of HEAD, §5.6.0a step 5); the paid runs used it.

#### 5.6.6 The real runs

| Arm | Checkout | Database | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline, run 1 and run 2 | baseline | `calib_base` | `run_baseline_arm.py --run 1` / `--run 2` |
| new uncached | new | `calib_new` | `run_new_arm.py --arm new_uncached` |
| new with question-group caches | new | `calib_new` | `run_new_arm.py --arm new_cached` |
| new on the fallback model (200) | new | `calib_new` | `run_new_arm.py --arm new_fallback --ids calib/ids_200.json` |

Use the step-5 commands without `--dry-run`, with a new `--out` for each run (e.g. `calib/baseline_1.jsonl`). Order: baseline 1, baseline 2, then the new arms.
- **new_uncached** grades through the individual re-score path, which never uses a group cache.
- **new_cached** grades through the bulk path. First set the engineer switch on `calib_new`: system parameter **`assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache` = `groups`** (since Q3, unset already means `groups`; `synthetic.py` sets it anyway). The arm groups each candidate's answers with the code's own `_cache_plan` and runs at concurrency 1 (R6-03). Each row records whether `cachedContent` was sent: all `false` means the cache path was not taken and the arm is just a second uncached run (expected on prod-shaped 2-question papers - B3-15). Without W13 in the checkout, skip it.
- **new_fallback** uses the configured fallback model (`gemini-2.5-pro`), or `--model`. Prod has none configured (B1-09). Skipped on 2026-09-24 for that reason.
- Limits: calls paced to `vertex_max_rpm`, or 60/min when unset; concurrency 4; a run stops starting calls at `--max-usd` (default $40); the per-candidate cap does not apply (this spend is not the candidate's); the daily cap still reads the copy's ledger. `run_arm` refuses any non-dry run on a live or unblanked database unless every answer sits on a synthetic paper (R6-09, FU14). The bearer is minted on its own cursor and renewed 300 s before expiry, so a long run holds no lock (R6-04). A result file is never overwritten: if a run dies, rerun that arm with a new `--run` number and `--out`.

#### 5.6.7 Compare

```bash
python3 $T/compare.py calib/baseline_1.jsonl calib/baseline_2.jsonl calib/new_*.jsonl --out calib/report.md
```

Reading the report:
- **Arms table**: rows compared and rows excluded, with the reason for each. Excluded = not graded by the model (gated or verdict-only), not `scored` (e.g. a truncated labelling reply), or served by another model than the arm asked for (the fallback stepped in). Many exclusions in one arm is a finding in itself.
- **Verdict per question type**: **wobble** = baseline run 1 vs run 2; **MAD** = the new arm's mean absolute difference from the mean of the two baseline runs; **drift** = mean signed difference, with a sign-test p; **flips** = pass/fail changes at each assessment's pass bar.
- **PASS** = MAD <= wobble MAD and p >= 0.05. An arm passes only when every type passes. Round 1 (B3-24): there is no minimum count - with 2 answers a two-sided sign test cannot go below p = 0.5, so tiny types pass on noise; report INSUFFICIENT for any type under the minimum and make the overall verdict INCOMPLETE. Superseded 2026-09-24 (R6-05): built - a type with fewer than 20 answers (`MIN_PER_TYPE`) in the arm or in the wobble is INSUFFICIENT, a type the baseline never scored included, and the arm's verdict is then INCOMPLETE, never PASS.
- **On made-up answers** the wobble is tiny (marks are mostly 0 or 100 at temperature 0.2), so small moves FAIL the MAD rule. Read the direction by answer kind as well (§5.6.10).
- **Labelling box flips**: boxes crossing the pass bar, vs the wobble's own flips.
- **Caps fired**: how often the fabrication, checklist and contradiction caps fired, per arm and type. A jump in fabrication on the new arms means the "not confirmed, not contradicted" rule is not being followed.
- **Tokens and cost**: real spend per arm, and how many calls sent `cachedContent`.
- **Trick answers**, per arm (`F` = fabrication cap fired): invented earns nothing and is not marked fabrication on the new arms; contradicting loses marks on every arm; true_unlisted is not punished.
- Why the mean: if the new request is exactly as noisy as today's, its MAD from the baseline mean lands ~13% under the wobble MAD - the room the PASS rule needs. Simulated false-FAIL rate: 23% at 30 answers per type, 9% at 100. The sign test adds 5% per type and arm. A lone FAIL with p just under 0.05 and MAD inside the wobble is usually noise: rerun that arm once as `--run 2` before changing anything.

#### 5.6.8 On FAIL

- **new_uncached fails a type:** adjust the instructions (`prompts/scoring.md` plus the identical `DEFAULT_SCORING_PROMPT`) or that type's fields (`services/scoring.py` `_question_material`). Rerun the **new arms only** (the baseline files stay valid; baseline code has not changed). Compare again. Nothing ships until every type passes.
- **Only new_cached fails:** ship with the cache switch **off** (set `scoring_cache` = `off`) and tell the owner. Superseded 2026-09-24: "(the code default)" - the default is now `groups` (Q3).
- **Drift one way:** the new request is consistently harsher or softer. Check the caps table and the trick outcomes for the cause before rewriting.
- **new_fallback fails:** report it to the owner (the fallback retires on 2026-10-20; replacement chosen later; prod has none set).

#### 5.6.9 Afterwards

- `dropdb calib_base calib_new`, then delete both filestore copies.
- The JSONL files hold answer ids and scores only. Keep the report and delete the rest.
- **Future model swaps:** rerun `run_new_arm.py --arm new_uncached --model <candidate> --run N` against fresh baseline runs of the code then in prod, and compare the same way.
- Synthetic mode: drop the synthetic database too (it keeps its source's `hr.applicant` rows). `etp_f2_synth` still holds 262 real, blanked answers; the harness refuses it until `synthetic.py` is re-run (Part 0 §0.9).

#### 5.6.10 Synthetic calibration record (2026-09-24)

Three paid runs, each on a synthetic database built as in §5.6.0a (made-up answers only; the Vertex keys blanked again and the database dropped afterwards). Model `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` and temperature 0.2 on both sides, unchanged. Old prompt = HEAD `bundled:34c42d2f`.

| Run | New prompt | Scope | Calls | Cost | $ per answer, new (old) | `compare.py` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `bundled:f8a15cce` | 110 answers: old prompt twice, new uncached, new cached | 22 per arm, plus 2 retried (one 429, one 500) and 1 cache create | $8.38 | 0.0164 uncached, 0.0155 cached (0.0216, 0.0226) | FAIL, both arms, every type |
| 2 | `bundled:11b900fb` | the same 110: new uncached, new cached (old runs reused) | 22 per arm | $3.78 | 0.0178 uncached, 0.0165 cached | FAIL, except image_label in the cached arm |
| 3 | `bundled:785826a5` | 46 targeted answers, new uncached only; image_ab left out | 16 | $1.09 | 0.0238 (0.0214, 0.0220 on the same 46) | INCOMPLETE: 10-14 answers per type, minimum 20 |

Total $13.25, billed to a non-prod Vertex project (Q2b had allowed prod's). Run 3 stayed under its $1.22 stop (budget guard in the run wrapper).

**By answer kind** (new against the mean of the two old runs):

| Kind | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Correct | same (20/20 pass) | same (20/20) | same (16/16; mean 98.8 vs 98.8) |
| Partial | same overall; image_prompt harsher (50 -> 35-38; #44865 40 -> 0) | harsher (-4.0 / -2.7; #44895 70 -> 20; #44925 80 -> 60) | #44895 back to 70, #44925 to 80; **#44865 still 0 (old 40)**; mean 40 vs 50; 2 of 4 pass, as old |
| Wrong | **worse**: #44929 (the right defects under the wrong box numbers) 0 -> 100, passing; #44958 ("both are good") 0 -> 38 | fixed: both 0 | same (0) |
| Off-topic | slightly better (an image_ab answer about lighting 25 -> 0) | slightly better | not in scope |
| Note to the grader | same resistance, a little more lenient; the fabrication cap stopped firing (#44909 25 -> 50) | 2 of 15 above old (#44908 18-20 vs 10; #44909 50 vs 25) | none above old; much stricter (mean 6.2 vs 22.8; 9 of 12 at 0) |
| Near-blank | a little worse ("bird doodle" #44886 0 -> 20) | #44886 30 in one arm | none above old (mean 4.2 vs 4.6; #44886 back to 0; #44943 50, as old) |
| Internal words in what the candidate reads | 6-9 of 110 vs 33-36 old | 13-19 of 110 vs 28-29 old | 1 of 46 (a plain-English "key") vs 11 of 46 old |

The word lists differ by run (run 1 counted "mandatory" too; runs 2-3 counted "official"), so compare within a run.

**What was fixed between the runs**
- Round 1 (`f8a15cce` -> `11b900fb`): an answer with no real content scores 0; text addressed to the grader earns nothing and counts as a fabrication; when the task asks for a decision, an answer that does not make one scores 0; on image_label, without `markers_hidden` a label counts only for the box it was written under, and a defect keyed for another box scores near 0; prompt elements are marked hit or miss one by one, each miss its own deduction, and a partial answer never collapses to 0 unless a keyed penalty says so; the plain-words rule covers the verdict too.
- Round 2 (`11b900fb` -> `785826a5`, 6 lines): near-blank scores 0 "even if the key would give some marks automatically" (#44886); a note to the grader "is its own deduction" (#44908); an element the answer conveys is a hit "even without every detail; a vague, wrong or absent one is a miss" (#44895, #44865); `fabrication_count` is now reported on image_label, counting only text addressed to the grader, so the 25 cap can fire on injected labels (#44909; the box scores still decide the mark); the plain-words rule says what to write instead and bans "rubric", "golden", "official", "keyed", "Major issue", "the key", "the model answer" and "a score cap". 177 grading and prompt tests passed after it (36 classes).
- Size: `f8a15cce` 7,197 chars; `11b900fb` 8,095; `785826a5` 8,451 (about +89 tokens per call over round 1). The old prompt is about 18,400 chars.

**Not like prod:** prod calls carry 2 answers (these carried 5; run 3 had 6 single-answer calls); one made-up answer per pattern, so each cell rests on 3-4 answers; the video questions were graded without clips on both sides, as prod does.

**Open after run 3** (owner call, Part 0 §0.1): partial image and video prompt answers can score lower than on the old prompt (#44865); cost per answer on run 3 was 8-11% above the old prompt on the same 46 answers, not like-for-like. The Q2 spot check covers the first paper graded under the new prompt. The reports and per-answer files stay in the session's scratch folder, not in the repo.

### 5.7 Manual test script - everything in 19.0.3.22.0

Hands-on QA of waves 1-2 (archive & delete, hardening, settings parity). Every step has the exact value to type and the exact thing to look for. Follow top to bottom: each paper you build is reused later. Budget ~45 minutes. **Expected** lines in bold are the assertion - if what you see differs by more than whitespace, that is a finding.

Notes for use after 19.0.3.23.0: 9b.1, 9b.2 and the "Same questions for everybody" half of 9b.3 are superseded by W7 (the switch is gone from both UIs; every paper draws one shared set). 9a.1's 429 only fires where `base.login_cooldown_after` > 0 - it is 0 on prod (B5-08).

There is no Archive button in the form header - that is the Flutter console. Archived records are hidden from the list until you switch on **Filters > Archived**.

../.venv/bin/python odoo-bin -c ../src/odoo.conf -d etp_local \

#### 5.7.2 The launch fix - a roster built in the UI must launch

(No one-click "Create" - the field sets `no_quick_create`, because a candidate with no email cannot get an exam link or a login; Email is required.)

#### 5.7.3 The exam gate - what archiving does and does NOT do

Archiving **suspends background work** (grading, invitations, the closed-tab expiry sweep). It does **not** stop the clock, does **not** close the paper for somebody sitting it, and gives nobody time back on restore (`deadline_datetime` = `started_at + duration_minutes`, never touched). An earlier version of this script asserted the opposite; the assertions below are the corrected ones.

3.1 Sit the exam: private window, paste the link, sign in as `qa.sitter.one@example.com` with the default candidate password, go to the first question. **Expected:** the prompt `What must happen before charging a battery?`. Type any answer and submit it. **Leave this window open, mid-exam.**

3.2 The console refuses to archive a paper somebody is sitting:
- Flutter console, open `QA-1 Launch`, **Archive**. **Expected: refused, with a count** - *"1 candidate(s) are sitting this right now. Archiving does not pause their exam and does not give time back - each one is still submitted at their original deadline."*
- Confirm it (sends `confirm_live_attempts`). **Expected:** it archives.

3.3 Archive from Odoo (the cog Archive has no confirmation; it writes `active` directly and the model catches that write):
- Odoo, `QA-1 Launch`, **gear > Unarchive**, then **gear > Archive**. **Expected:** an **Archived** ribbon.
- Candidate window, continue/refresh. **Expected: the exam is STILL OPEN**, same question. Correct, not a finding.
- **Settings > Technical > Scheduled Actions**. **Expected:** `_cron_llm_auto_score`, `_cron_send_pending_invitations`, `_cron_expire_stale_attempts` all still `Active` (archive makes the cron skip this assessment, it does not disable it).
- Assessment header **Scoring** badge. **Expected:** **Not Scoring** (`idle`), not *Stopping*, although archiving raised the cancel flag.
- **Run Subjective Evaluation** on the archived paper, wait two minutes. **Expected: nothing graded, no Vertex spend.** Rows keep `scoring_requested` / `llm_state` untouched, so an unarchive resumes with no replay.

3.4 Restore: **gear > Unarchive**. **Expected:** queued grading resumes on the next cron tick, from the same rows. The candidate was never interrupted.

#### 5.7.4 Archive excludes it everywhere

4.1 Record the "before":

| Where | What to note |
|---|---|
| **Assessments v2 > Dashboard** | the ASSESSMENTS, CANDIDATES, PASSED, FAILED tiles |
| **All Responses** (top menu) | number of groups, and the **Total Objective** footer |
| Dashboard > **Candidates** tile > row `QA Sitter One` | the **Assessments** tile and the number of rows in **Assessment History** |

4.2 Archive `QA-1 Launch` again and re-read. **Expected:** every dashboard tile drops by this paper's contribution; the paper's group leaves All Responses **and the Total Objective footer drops** by its marks; on the candidate profile the **Assessments tile and the Assessment History row count still equal each other**, both one lower (the sharpest check: the tile used to exclude archived papers while the table listed them). **Unarchive** and confirm every number returns.

5.2 The advice changes once archived: archive `QA-1 Launch`, tick it (Archived filter on), **Actions > Delete**. **Expected:** same refusal, advice **"This one is already archived, so it is ready: open it and use Delete Permanently."** Must NOT say *"archive it, open it"*, nor *"archiving alone is enough"*.

#### 5.7.9a The hardening wave (57 findings) - independent quick checks

9a.1 A rate-limited sign-in says so, and how long. POST a WRONG password 12 times:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' -X POST \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"jdata":{"login":"qa.sitter.one@example.com","password":"nope"}}' \
    http://localhost:8069/api/v1/auth_token
done; echo
```

**Expected:** the first few `400`, then **`429`**. With `-i`: a **`Retry-After`** header and *"Too many sign-in attempts from this network. Wait a minute and try again - your password is not the problem."* (Before, a rate-limited candidate was told to check correct credentials.) Then sign in as a DIFFERENT candidate (`qa.sitter.two@example.com`) with the correct password and retry the bad login. **Expected: still `429`** - a success clears only that candidate's own counter, never the shared per-IP counter (or spraying would never be limited); the IP counter ages out after `base.login_cooldown_duration`.

9a.2 A mixed-case login can sign in: **Settings > Users > New**, email `QA.Mixed.Case@Example.com`, any throwaway password, save, reopen. **Expected:** Login stored **`qa.mixed.case@example.com`**. Sign in as `QA.Mixed.Case@Example.com`. **Expected:** it works (exact match first, escaped `=ilike` fallback for legacy rows).

9a.3 The roster sort is honest: in the console roster click **SCORE** twice (descending). **Expected:** ranks by the **whole** mark - "16 / 20" above "5 / 20". Click **FLAG** on a cohort of 100+ and page to the end. **Expected:** every candidate exactly once (forced `id` tiebreaker; boolean columns tie ~700 rows).

9a.4 Out-of-range settings are refused everywhere: **Settings > Assessments v2**, **Scoring Shards** `8`, Save. **Expected:** refused by the form constraint (`_check_be_llm_limits`). Through the API:

```bash
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"scoring_shards": 8}' \
  http://localhost:8069/api/v1/settings/update
```

**Expected:** `422` naming the range **1-4**, the same range `tools/check_settings_in_range.py` uses (all three read `constants.SETTING_RANGES`). Then set **Thinking Level** to `MEDIUM` in the console Settings, Save, reopen **Odoo > Settings**. **Expected:** opens normally; console shows `MEDIUM` on reload. A lowercase `medium` must be refused at the door (it used to save 200 and break Odoo Settings with `Wrong value for ... 'medium'`).

9a.5 Exam tokens are not in the access log - sit an exam with a question image, then:

```bash
grep -c 'qimage' /path/to/odoo.log
grep 'qimage' /path/to/odoo.log | head -3
```

**Expected:** request lines present with the token segment **`<redacted>`**, on both `/assessments_be/exam/qimage/...` **and** `/pro_assessment/qimage/...`.

9a.6 A broken avatar renders a placeholder, not a 500: **Settings > Users**, scroll users incl. pre-April accounts. **Expected:** grey placeholder for a missing filestore file; no `500`, no `FileNotFoundError` traceback - one `INFO` line per row.

#### 5.7.9b Settings parity - one setting, one name (superseded in part by W7)

9b.1 Open any **draft** assessment in Odoo. **Expected (19.0.3.22.0):** a group **Scoring** with three switches in this order - **Same questions for everybody**, **Shuffle Questions**, **Grade subjective answers automatically** - in the console's wording; *Violations & Scoring* now **Violations** (violation action and cap only); no *Same Questions for Everyone*, *Keep bank order (do not shuffle)* or *Auto-queue subjective grading on submit*. *After 19.0.3.23.0 the first switch is gone (W7).* Tick **Shuffle Questions** off, Save, reopen. **Expected:** stays off; from the shell the stored column moved the other way:

```
env["assessments.be"].browse(ID).read(
    ["shuffle_questions", "preserve_question_order"])
# -> shuffle_questions False, preserve_question_order True
```

9b.2 A bare create draws one shared paper: **New**, name only, Save. **Expected (19.0.3.22.0):** **Same questions for everybody** ON; a pre-existing draft unchanged; scripts wanting independent draws must send `same_questions_for_all: false`. *Superseded by W7: the key is ignored and every paper draws one shared set.*

9b.3 The app locks what the server refuses: console, a **running** assessment's **Config** tab (operator with configure capability). **Expected:** **Shuffle Questions** locked (and, before W7, **Same questions for everybody**); **Grade subjective answers automatically** still editable, locked only on **Done** or **Cancelled**. Turn autograde ON on that running paper. **Expected:** an info Notice that it applies from the next submission onwards, naming **Re-score This Assessment** to sweep in those who already submitted; never on a draft or when the toggle is off.

#### 5.7.10 Clean up

1. Any paper with answers: **Archive**, open, **Delete Permanently**. 2. Empty papers: **Actions > Delete**. 3. **Questions**: delete `QA Q1 Battery`, `QA Q2 Ladder`, `QA Q3 Spare` (retire instead if a paper still references them). 4. **Generators**: delete `QA Manual Gen`. 5. **Settings > Users**: archive `QA Restricted`. 6. Candidates `QA Sitter One/Two` and the invitees can stay - ordinary applicant records, and 5.5's point is that deleting a paper does not remove them. Finally **Assessments** > Filters > **Archived** should be empty.

#### 5.7.11 What each section proves

| § | The change |
|---|---|
| 2 | Launch bug - a roster built in the UI could not be launched at all |
| 3 | Archiving suspends grading, invitations and the expiry sweep - and does NOT pause a sitting, stop the clock or close the exam. The console refuses it, with a count, while anyone is mid-paper |
| 4 | Archiving removes it from every figure and list; unarchiving restores them (round 1: the candidate's own "Closed" list still shows it - C3) |
| 5.1-5.2 | Delete refuses with counts, and the advice fits the paper's state |
| 5.3 | Invited-but-unstarted rosters now block instead of vanishing |
| 5.5 | Delete Permanently: archive-first, and what survives |
| 6 | `done` is final, and warns before you get there |
| 7 | Question deletes name what they would destroy |
| 8 | A restricted manager is told why the button is missing |
| 9 | Pace, tooltips, filters, Cancel gating, the rename, the corrected Mark Done tooltip |
| 9a | Hardening wave: the 429 refusal and its rolling per-IP window, case-folded logins, roster sort allow-list, one settings-range table, exam-token redaction, missing-filestore placeholder |
| 9b | Settings parity: one Scoring group in Flutter's words and order, the non-stored `shuffle_questions` mirror, the `same_questions_for_all` default flip (new records only; since retired by W7), the Config tab locking what the server refuses |

### 5.8 Post-deploy steps of the scoring-visibility release (2026-09-18, historical)

Run in this order at that deploy (deploying BEFORE re-queueing proves the fairness fix: all four papers go back in the queue together and must interleave):
1. Confirm the upgrade landed: any assessment form header carries a Scoring badge while a run is live; the list has a `Scoring` column.
2. Run Subjective Evaluation on assessment 57 (IG Entity), 44, 45 and 47. 486 candidates were parked by a kill on 2026-09-18 and 217 more on 57. Already-scored answers are excluded, so nothing is re-graded or re-billed. Budget: ~1,382 ungraded answers at ~$0.09 each, ~$124; daily cap $400, resets at UTC midnight; check LLM Budget first.
3. Watch the list `Scoring` column: all four papers move from Queued into Scoring. One sitting at Queued while another drains = the fairness fix did not take.
4. Watch the header badge on 57: refreshes every 3 s; the form reloads once when the run settles.
5. Kill Scoring Process disappears the moment a paper's queue empties (the reported bug closed).
6. A red "Grader Not Running" badge and danger alert = the scoring cron is inactive or >15 min overdue. Re-enable it under Settings > Technical > Scheduled Actions ("Assessments BE v2: Auto-score").

"No configuration change is required. `scoring_shards=4` and `scoring_tick_limit=20` are correct as they stand." - Superseded 2026-09-23: prod's tick limit is 5 (B1-08). Status of step 2 (B2-20): done for 44, 45 and 57; **not for 47**, where 53 candidates (101 answers) are still parked.

### 5.9 Locked-mode drive runbook (Safe Exam Browser)

For invigilators and lab prep (drafted 6 Oct 2026, S-07). Applies only to papers with "Require Safe Exam Browser" on; the rule is off by default. Rules come from Part 11 (§11.2-§11.6). "Learning N" and "S-NN" point into `new_work/items_to_do_seb.md`.

**Blocker: the Windows and Mac real-machine checks (S-03, S-04, §11.6) are not done. Do not switch the rule on for a real paper until both pass (S-18).** Until then, run steps 1-8 below only on a test paper.

**Before the drive (lab prep, a day ahead)**
1. Install Safe Exam Browser (SEB) on every lab PC: version 3.10 on Windows (10 1803+ or 11), 3.7 on macOS (12+). Part 11 was built against these; other versions are untested (§11.6).
2. macOS only: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera, allow Safe Exam Browser. Windows grants the camera on its own. SEB for macOS has open camera bugs (seb-mac #483, #602), so test it (learning 10).
3. Switch the rule on for the paper (admin or the assessment owner): tick "Require Safe Exam Browser" on the Odoo assessment form, or use its switch in the Flutter admin (§11.2 step 1). Only on a test paper until S-18 clears.
4. Set a FRESH quit password on the paper: Odoo assessment form, "Safe Exam Browser Quit Password" (shown once the rule is on; the Flutter admin shows it read-only, S-13). Write it on paper for invigilators only. Never reuse an old paper's value: after `-u` every older paper shares one generated password (learning 7, §11.5, S-06).
5. Do not change that password once candidates are inside SEB. It changes SEB's Config Key (SEB's settings fingerprint), so everyone inside is refused and must relaunch from the link (§11.5, learning 11). Toggling the webcam rule is safe: the camera is always allowed in the SEB settings (learning 11). (dev) Do not push a change to `seb.settings` mid-drive: it changes the Config Key too (S-09).
6. (admin) Confirm the system parameter `web.base.url` is the API host `https://projects.ethara.ai` on that database (Settings > Technical > System Parameters, developer mode). The `sebs://` launch link is built from it (§11.5, S-05).
7. Brief candidates in the room or by a separate notice that SEB is needed. The invitation email cannot mention proctoring (learning 12, test-enforced), so without a briefing they first hear at the gate. How candidates learn is open (S-08).
8. Dry-run one machine per OS end to end: the "On the day" steps through submit and Exit, then once more with a quit via the password.

**On the day (candidates)**
1. Open the invitation link (`/exam/<token>`) in a NORMAL browser, not in SEB.
2. The page shows "Open this assessment in Safe Exam Browser" with two buttons, "Open in Safe Exam Browser" and "Download Safe Exam Browser". No questions are shown (§11.2).
3. Press "Open in Safe Exam Browser". SEB downloads the paper's .seb file and starts locked to this paper.
4. Sign in INSIDE SEB, even if already signed in outside it. The SEB check runs before sign-in and SEB starts with fresh storage, so one sign-in is enough (learning 6).
5. Read the instructions and start as usual.
6. SEB missing: stay on the gate, press "Download Safe Exam Browser", install, press "Open in Safe Exam Browser" again. What Chrome or Safari show on Open when SEB is not installed is unconfirmed (S-10): if nothing visibly happens, treat SEB as not installed.

**During**
- Quit password (invigilator only): closes SEB before the candidate submits, for a fault or an early exit. Never read it out and never leave it where candidates can see it.
- Relaunch: if SEB closes, crashes or was quit, the candidate reopens the same link in a normal browser, presses "Open in Safe Exam Browser" again and signs in again inside SEB. The clock keeps running meanwhile (as built, from code, not in Part 11: the deadline is server-side, `started_at` plus the duration, and `/begin` never re-stamps `started_at`; `candidate.py` `exam_begin` docstring, `models/assessment.py::_compute_deadline_datetime` 5980-5987).
- Camera lost mid-exam (paper has Require webcam on). As built, from code, not in Part 11: the camera track ending fires a "Webcam turned off / lost" violation (`ethara-assessment-fe/lib/services/proctor_web.dart:782-790`) and the candidate gets a blocking "Your camera is off" screen with an "Enable camera" button (`exam_screen.dart:354-365`). Violations count toward the paper's Violation Limit (`max_violations`, default 5). With On Violation = "Auto-submit assessment" the exam ends at the limit; with "Log violation only" it never ends and only shows "Violation limit breached" (`violation_action` and `max_violations`, `models/assessment.py:650-671`). On a Mac check step 2 of the prep first. Note the SEB version on any camera failure (S-04).
- Not locked: question images and videos load outside the SEB check (§11.5, S-11). Phones and people are the invigilators' job.

**After**
- The candidate submits. The complete screen shows "Exit Safe Exam Browser" (`exam_screen.dart:3462`); pressing it goes to the quit URL, which should close SEB with no password. Not proven on a real machine yet (§11.6, S-03, S-04): if SEB does not close, use the quit password.
- Collect nothing from the candidate or the PC: answers and violations are already on the server. Keep the quit password paper with the invigilators.
- Next drive on the same paper: set a new quit password first (step 4 of the prep). Log any failure with the SEB version in Part 11 §11.6.

### 6.1 Wave 1 - Archive & delete (18 Sep 2026)

**The problem.** An operator had two ways to make an assessment go away, and both lied.
- **"Archive" did almost nothing.** It hid the paper from 2 admin screens out of ~30. Marks still counted in every dashboard figure, the leaderboard, pass rates and averages; invitations still went out; grading still ran - an archived paper kept spending real money on Vertex, because the crons search the attempt table and `assessments.be.evaluator` has no `active` column. (Candidates could still sit an archived paper - unchanged and deliberate.)
- **"Delete" was refused, always**, with advice that could not be followed ("reset it to draft first", impossible for a finished paper). So nothing could be removed.

**What was delivered.**
- **Archive suspends an assessment:** queued invitations stand down, pending grading stops, the closed-tab expiry sweep is suspended (the three crons skip an archived paper). The one Vertex call on the wire completes and is billed; every call after it is refused. It leaves every figure and list: dashboard tiles, charts, leaderboard, candidate profiles, attempts and answers listings, scoring queue, back-office Responses menu, the candidate's own view (superseded 2026-09-23: attempt 10435 on an archived paper still shows under "Closed" - C3). Every result is kept, nothing is snapshotted; unarchiving resumes from the same rows.
- **What archiving does NOT do** (an earlier draft claimed the opposite): it does not pause a sitting, stop the clock, or close the exam. `deadline_datetime` = `started_at + duration_minutes`, an absolute instant archiving never touches; candidate gates test `state`, not `active`. A candidate mid-paper carries on and is auto-submitted at the original deadline. Restoring gives nobody time back. So **archiving is refused while anyone is sitting the paper**, by name and number: *"12 candidate(s) are sitting this right now. Archiving does not pause their exam and does not give time back."* The PII retention sweep is deliberately **not** suspended: retention is a legal duty with its own clock. A paper that must STOP is cancelled or marked done.
- **Delete exists, guarded:** "Delete Permanently" destroys an assessment, its attempts and answers, offered **only on an archived paper** (the counts in the confirmation cannot change while read). Candidate accounts, bank questions and the generator always survive. Ordinary Delete still refuses anything holding candidate data, but says exactly what it protects (answers, candidates, papers) and names a route that works.
- **Three further protections:** invitations count as something to lose (a launched paper with a full roster and no answers used to delete behind a generic "are you sure", breaking every invited link - now refused and counted); "finished" is final in fact (a finished paper could be forced back through the API into a state where a destructive reset was available, with no confirmation or audit trail); a read can no longer create data (opening an expired attempt on a closed paper used to manufacture blank answers).
- **Wording:** question deletion reports answers, candidates, papers and submitted sittings at stake; "Reset to Draft" renamed **"Clear and Reset to Draft"**; **"Mark Done" asks for confirmation** in Odoo; restricted managers are told why Delete Permanently is missing.

**Bugs found in QA (pre-existing, fixed):** (a) assessments built in the Odoo UI could not be launched - "Please assign at least one candidate before starting" while the candidate was visibly in the roster; the assessment stored candidates in two places and only one was kept in step; (b) the "Mark Done" tooltip said candidates "keep their remaining time" - they are closed out immediately; now correct, with a test preventing drift.

**Risk and deploy (then):** no migration (the one added field is a non-stored compute); no existing data invalidated (the `done` restriction applies to attempted changes, never records at rest); deploy must run `-u assessments_be_v2`. Deliberate behaviour changes, all refusing where something previously succeeded silently: (1) deleting an assessment whose only content is unstarted invitations blocks and counts them; (2) a finished assessment can no longer be pushed back to "cancelled" through the API; (3) archiving a paper someone is sitting is refused unless `confirm_live_attempts`; (4) repeated failed sign-ins from one network answer **429** rather than 400 - brute-force protection "back ON" (superseded 2026-09-23: prod has the cooldown at 0 since 2026-09-17, so it never fires - B5-08); the client honours `Retry-After`; (5) out-of-range scheduler settings refused on the Odoo form as well as the API; (6) new logins containing `@` stored lower-cased.

### 6.2 Wave 2 - The 57-finding hardening wave (18 Sep 2026)

A 17-dimension adversarial review produced 94 raw findings; **57 were confirmed by two independent refutation agents each** and fixed, each with a test proven red when the fix is reverted. Full structured set: `findings.json` from that review run (outside the module; field notes and handoffs in `/Users/cj/Developer/etp-test-650-observability`).

By theme:
- **Sign-in under a shared ingress IP.** Brute-force protection keyed on the **login** (`res.users._assert_can_auth`), not `remote_addr`: every candidate reaches Odoo as one of two ingress addresses, so Odoo's per-IP bucket was effectively global - five failures froze a 753-candidate cohort (3,668 refusals in seven minutes) and protection was switched off. A second, 20x-looser per-IP bucket still catches one host spraying many accounts; it is a **rolling window**, and a success deliberately does **not** clear it. Policy stays Odoo's (`base.login_cooldown_after` / `_duration`; `0` disables). Bucket bounded at 4,096 entries (oldest-half eviction). Superseded 2026-09-23: prod still has both at 0, so no limit applies (B5-08).
- **A rate-limited candidate is no longer told their password is wrong.** `POST /api/v1/auth_token` answers **429 with `Retry-After`** and "your password is not the problem", classified through the shared predicate `res.users._be_login_cooldown_key`. Cited as the cause of **679 password-reset emails** on the 753-candidate run (superseded 2026-09-23: prod shows 693 on 17 Sep, ~78% after the limiter was switched off - B5-09). The header matters: without it one refusal became five retries.
- **Mixed-case logins.** `res.users.create` folds any `@`-shaped login to lower case; the gateway falls back to an escaped `=ilike` for legacy rows. "53 of 1,663 production logins unreachable" (superseded 2026-09-23: 52 are self-signup portal accounts from 29 Apr, 40+ with injection-payload logins; forgot-password still matches the lower-cased email exactly - B5-19).
- **One number per fact.** `vertex.spend_cap` is the ONE spend-cap resolver (gate, LLM Budget dashboard, Settings route) - with rows absent the screens said `cap_usd: 0, capped: false` while the gate refused every call at $100/day, and the console posts all four governance keys on any Save, so one Save disabled the cap. `constants.SETTING_RANGES` is the ONE range table (form constraint, write API, pre-deploy gate; the gate's copy had drifted and refused a stored `0`). `assessments.be._scoring_drainer_health()` is the ONE definition of "the grader is dead" (Odoo badge and `GET /api/v1/scoring`).
- **A method silently composed away.** `res_config_settings._check_llm_limits` renamed **`_check_be_llm_limits`**: `etp_assessment_pro` defines the plain name on the same model with no `super()`, so on prod none of v2's settings checks ran. Three more collisions renamed: `_onchange_vertex_sa_upload`, `_onchange_question_prompt_upload`, `_onchange_scoring_prompt_upload` -> `_onchange_be_*`, and `_decode_upload` -> `_be_decode_upload` (uploads always persisted via `set_values`; only live in-form feedback was lost). Static guard `tests/test_a_shared_model_has_no_shared_method_names.py` parses BOTH modules with `ast` (the suite's DB has `etp_assessment_pro` uninstalled).
- **Scoring phase cannot latch:** `stopping` requires something running or queued; `_scoring_drainer_health` counts only shards that are supposed to run.
- **Diagnosis where there was none:** exam media 404s log which of five faults occurred (unknown token, different candidate, no assessment role, deleted row, question not drawn) and never the token; exam tokens redacted from the werkzeug access log incl. legacy `/pro_assessment/{qimage,qvideo}/<token>/<id>`; a blocked launch names the failing gates; every candidate who cannot be provisioned is named at once, each in its own savepoint (a 652-row roster with 172 portal addresses used to import nobody and name one person); one audit line per exam action and per refusal.
- **Roster sorting:** `sort` / `sort_desc` through a nine-column allow-list (`admin.py::_SORTABLE`) with a forced `id` tiebreaker; `score` maps to **`score_percent`** (sorting by the MCQ sub-total put "16 / 20" below "5 / 20"). Two stored columns (`candidate_name`, `state_rank`) back the CANDIDATE and STATE headers; both backfill on `-u`.
- **A missing filestore file answers a placeholder, not a 500:** 1,054 attachments point at files that no longer exist after the `location = db` switch (2,483 tracebacks, 5 hard 500s on the 753-candidate run). Rows **not** repaired - separate decision; `force_storage()` must not be used.
- **Settings parity:** Part 4 §4.8.

|---|---|
| `api_auth_gateway/controllers/main.py` | `auth_token` answers 429 + `Retry-After` for a cooldown refusal instead of 400; `_is_rate_limited` asks BOTH `registry._login_failures` and `res.users._be_login_cooldown_key`; `_cooldown_seconds` reads `base.login_cooldown_duration`, clamped 1-3600; `readonly=False` (the route mints a token; `auth='none'` defaults read-only); `login` bound before the `try` (so the error handler cannot die on `UnboundLocalError`); inputs coerced with `str()` (the shared validator skips `{'type': 'str'}`); exact-match lookup first, escaped `=ilike` fallback |
