### 6.4 Wave 3 - W1-W16 (22-23 Sep 2026), 19.0.3.23.0

**State:** built, merged and tested; staged backend diff + uncommitted app tree. Built by 8 parallel lanes, then caching + calibration tooling, then a 5-angle review (production safety, grading concurrency, API contract, Odoo UI in a real browser, grading request) and a fix round for every finding. ~87 backend and ~43 app files touched; 36 new or changed backend test files, 22 app test files (at the audit: 96 files / +12,945 / -1,753 by `git diff HEAD --stat`; now 124 staged files).

| Area | What changed |
|---|---|
| Login | `en-GB` browsers no longer get "session expired": an uninstalled language is swapped for an installed one before any ORM call (W1) |
| Grading collisions | no lane writes the shared paper row; outlier staleness derived from data; recompute writes only flips; rollback after a serialization failure; bearer on its own cursor (W2). Local synthetic stress run: 793 wasted calls -> 0 (not prod - B1-05) |
| Kill / lanes | Kill sees and settles a candidate being graded; never parks a row a live lane holds; a dead lane's row is parked; lane-lock health; connection budget counts the lane's own connections (3 calls/lane at a pool of 64) (W3, W5) |
| Individual re-score | queued per click (`rescore_request_key`), graded first and alone; a mark replaced only when the new grade succeeds; Kill clears requests; "Re-score All" removed; per-answer / selected re-score grade exactly the chosen answers; admin buttons skip candidates being graded (W6) |
| Grading request | text-only; only what scoring needs (task incl. description, rubric/golden, axes + official reasoning, box keys + decoys, required elements + penalties + scoring guide + reference prompt); trimmed reply; rules by question type with a mismatch flag; override removed (stored value left, unread); output floor 16k, retry doubles up to the model limit; token pinned with expiry (W12) |
| Caching | question-group caches for bulk runs only, answers never cached, engineer switch `assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache` (default `off`; superseded 2026-09-23 by Q3: default `groups`) (W13) |
| Calibration | `tools/calibration/` + runbook: read-only arms, compare with a wobble rule, prompt-version and old-verdict prechecks (W15) |
| Admin console | Scored / Score Pending chips (Flutter only - B4-15); "same questions" retired (column kept) + count locked after launch; imports like Flutter (drafts first); Form Studio forms read-only in Odoo, Publish always, publish warnings; Question Templates on the generator; badge polling backoff (W4, W7-W11) |
| App | IST everywhere (times labelled, dates as the India date); verdict shown to candidates after release; email + copy button on their own line; launch warning for questions without a usable key; Settings shows parallel calls and scoring model in use; polling backoff and hidden-tab pause |

**New system parameters:** `assessments_be_v2.verdict_requires_current_prompt` (default on; absent = on) - Part 5 §5.2; `assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache` (default off; superseded 2026-09-23 by Q3: default `groups`); `assessments_be_v2.score_outlier_checks_since` (set by the first recompute run). Changed: `assessments_be_v2.scoring_parallel_calls` (code default 4). Removed: the scoring-prompt override. Full switch table: Part 0 §0.5 J.

**Decided (import):** CSV and harness JSON arrive as drafts in Pending Approvals; a native JSON bank export restores straight into the live bank (same rule for the file lane, the API payload lane and both UIs); the Odoo button reads "Restore into the bank" and asks first for that format (Part 4 §4.4).

**Audit fix round (2026-09-23).** All 9 high and 36 medium audit findings were worked in a second round: per-finding status and round-1 notes in Part 7 §7.2, the re-score contract changes in Part 3 §3.8, the owner decisions in Part 1 §1.2. Round 1 found 4 of them only partly fixed and 1 regressed (Part 7 §7.1). Tests: Odoo 2,300 / 2,300, Flutter 1,950 / 1,950 as reported then; re-counted 2026-09-23: Flutter 1,948 passed + 1 skipped (G6-01).

Superseded 2026-09-23: the summary's instruction "set the gate to `0` after the calibration precheck's verdict scan comes back clean" - do not (Part 5 §5.2). Round-1 validation then found 5 blockers in this wave (Part 1 §1.4.1).

**Final round (2026-09-23 evening to 2026-09-24).** The owner locked the plan (Q1-Q19, Part 0 §0.0). Seven lanes built it in parallel worktrees (backend API, lanes, grading, Odoo UI, tools; Flutter admin and candidate), each checked by a reviewer and fixed where the review found a problem, then merged into the main trees. Then: 9 review follow-ups, a gate (0 failed of 2,389 with crons on and off), the deploy-order matrix on the final code, three paid synthetic calibration runs with two prompt rewording rounds, 5 small leftovers, and the final gate (Odoo 2,391 / 0 failed / 1 error, Flutter 1,988 passed). Every M, S and N item is done (Part 0 §0.2). Prompt fingerprint `bundled:785826a5`; cache ON by default; the calibration tools ship.

**Round 3 (2026-09-24, after the Q20 follow-ups).** The final sign-off (read-only review RV1-RV6, hands-on UI checks MT1-MT3) found 5 regressions in our own work (RV1-01, RV1-02, RV3-01, RV4-01, RV6-01) and prod-side problems at time-up and in the Responses list (MT3-01, MT3-02, MT2FA-02). The owner approved "A-E as listed" plus A-074, A-133 and A-092 from the approvals register (Part 10). Built in lanes on detached worktrees (`etp-lanes/be-g3-*`, `fe-g3-*`), reviewed backend and Flutter independently, fixed, merged, then checked by hand in headless Chrome. Main changes: the 10 s answer grace and `server_now`; time-up is never a proctoring event; `/emails` limited to assessment mail; Reset to Draft guarded for released results; every upload sized before decoding; strict candidate addresses; no paid re-grade of unchanged A/B re-posts and no attempt spent without a call; the admin quick wins; and the violation rule the owner set on 24 Sep (Log only never ends the paper and labels a reached limit; Auto-submit ends it; default 5). Same version, no migration, no new column; left unstaged on top of the staged release. After a first docs pass, a Flutter fix-up pass (and one backend change) closed the gaps it found between the change record and the code. Final gate on the merged code: Odoo 2,443 tests, 0 failed, 0 errors; Flutter 2,037 passed with nothing skipped, 1,361 on Chrome; `flutter analyze` clean. Every item, the verification and what was not done: Part 0, Round 3 addendum.

**Round 3 follow-up (24-25 Sep 2026).** The owner's final violation rule: only Auto-submit ends the paper at the limit; Log only never does, even at the cap; in both modes a reached limit shows "Violation Limit Breached" to the candidate and the admin (A-074 and L-107 are one flow). Code: `violation_limit_breached` now true in both modes (cap 0 = the first violation under Auto-submit, never under Log only); the candidate's completion screen states it in both modes; the Odoo "Limit Breached" column and badge, the invitation lines and every help text follow; the Odoo field `max_violations` reads "Violation Limit"; new papers start at Log only + 5 (model defaults, API create fallback, both New Assessment forms; existing papers unchanged); new test `test_owners_case_log_only_cap_20_never_ends`. Round 3 is now staged except the relabel. `etp_local` was upgraded 19.0.3.22.0 -> 19.0.3.23.0 locally (backup first), the rig was repointed to `~/Developer/ethara/`, and the round-3 lanes and `etp_g3_*` databases were removed. Tests so far: Odoo 0 failed of 2,446; Flutter 2,041 passed; `flutter analyze` clean. Product testing and the final gate: Part 0, Round 3 addendum. Superseded 2026-09-25: "Log only never ends the paper and labels a reached limit; Auto-submit ends it; default 5" (the label was Log only only, and the model's default action was Auto-submit).

**Status 30 Sep:** separated from the Safe Exam Browser work (a later commit) and staged on its own in both repos as `19.0.3.24.0`; release summary in `ETP_KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md` 5.0a. Deploy order: `-u` from the new image before rolling the pods, then the app.

Deploy: rebuild the backend image (Pillow), owner runs `-u assessments_be_v2` (new columns `sop_gen_started_at`, `sop_gen_finished_at`, `tag_extract_reply`; mail template; golden->sample move and generated-text repair run from `init()`), rebuild the app.

- **Candidate-facing:** no pass mark in the invitation email or on the exam start screen (My Performance keeps it); email sign-in and "Before you start:" wording; no proctoring paragraph in the email; no hint text in any candidate answer box ("JUSTIFICATION (REQUIRED)" label instead); the released answer sheet shows the numbered (annotated) plate for labelling questions; side-free (Yes/No) comparisons show Left/Right images, not Response A/B.
- **Generation:** live generation stats (§4.9, option A) with Retry failed images; image/video crons woken when a run finishes; draft-template budget 4000 -> 12000 and `verify_planted_flaws` 4000 -> 12000; 429 on draft template -> 503 busy; golden and sample questions are one list (generation: SAMPLE format; Draft from SOP: rule 9); `.markdown` extracted; rationale/official reasoning kept consistent with the key after the random A/B swap; Yes/No official reasoning built from the key; `{type}` template slots filled; admin rename of image_ab ratings keeps `flaw_plan_json.construction_keys` in step; stuck `finalizing` runs settled after 15 minutes.
- **Robustness:** NUL/UTF-16 uploads stored clean (all text imports); transient DB errors retried (image render, tag extraction with the paid reply kept, label detection, SOP generation, invite cron); image_ab prose before a verdict and rubric prose with blank ratings held as drafts; Chromium launch under Odoo's RLIMIT_AS fixed in `dom_capture.py`; Pillow 10.2.0 -> 10.4.0; Veo zero-token rows no longer warn.
- **Console:** question count follows the ticked questions; generator edits re-read only that generator; `/attempts` `changed_since` + `meta.server_time`; public `/api/v1/auth/password_policy` with a live rules checklist on reset and change-password; the URL carries page, record, tab and filters, so Reload and Back/Forward keep the place.
- **Research parity:** generation no longer sends a GOLDEN EXAMPLES heading (owner decision); the scoring system prompt is deliberately byte-identical (its fingerprint gates candidate-visible verdicts) and side-free comparisons are described in the item data instead.
- **Labelling (q1170), owner rules 2026-09-29:** (1) Pictures are AI-made. A live website screenshot only for a generator with the new "Screenshot live websites" switch (`image_label_live_capture`, off by default; meant for High Res Dense); if that page cannot be captured, the AI picture is used and the draft says why. Without the switch the generation prompt asks for no website and any URL is dropped. (2) ONE box list per question, and the boxes drawn, answer key (`behavioural_key_json`), rubric `ideal_labels` and golden `solution_json` are all written from it (`prompt._apply_label_list` / `_label_key_vals`). The list comes from one method: NAMED boxes first (the generator's elements, placed on the rendered picture by one vision call, `vertex.locate_label_elements`; elements not on the picture are dropped from every carrier), else DETECTED boxes (vision's own, when the locate call fails or finds fewer than half; the rubric's `mandatory_elements`/`penalty_rules` are dropped because they described the replaced boxes). A live capture's own list also rewrites the rubric and golden. (3) One overlay everywhere (exam, answer sheet, bank, draft preview) via `services/labelling.label_overlay`; this fixed candidates on 1170 getting 17 inputs while graded on a 4-box key. Approval carries a website URL only when the approved picture is the capture. Local check: 10 of 10 named boxes placed on a real DuckDuckGo screenshot. New column: needs `-u`.
- **Image labelling end-to-end run (local, 2026-09-29):** Egocentric SOP + common-error CSV (AI pictures) and High Res Dense SOP + golden.docx (live websites), 4 image_label questions each. All 8 rendered; AI: 4 of 4 named boxes placed (6/4/5/4 boxes); websites: 4 captured. Every draft's drawn boxes, key, geometry, golden and rubric agree; one overlay each; approved 7620 (AI) and 7622 (web) keep the same numbering in the bank and exam. Bug found and fixed: eBay served its error page to the capture browser (1 box) and it was accepted - a capture with fewer than 3 controls is now a failed capture (`dom_capture.unusable_reason`), so the AI picture is used. Open: generated question text points at the SOP ("according to the SOP", "Refer to the SOP") - flagged on all 8, approval needs acknowledgement; captured keys are mechanical ("Opens Learn More"); an invisible carousel link was boxed on SoundCloud. Spend: $1.15 (AI flow), $0.43 (web flow).
- **Questions never point at the SOP (owner, 2026-09-30):** candidates do not have the SOP in the exam. The generation rule now says samples are for format only and their SOP pointers ("Refer to the SOP for...", "SOP section 6") must never be copied; then, before drafts are written, every string that still points at the SOP (name, question text, reasoning, rubric, picture key, golden rationale) is rewritten in ONE small call (`vertex._rewrite_source_references`), keeping only rewrites that no longer point at it. Options, correct answers and key verdicts are never rewritten (the key matches them exactly); the draft warning stays as the last net. Real run: 4 of 4 new drafts clean, no warnings; High Res Dense needed the rewrite (its golden.docx carries the pointer, $0.009), Egocentric did not. The unused `_GEN_SELF_CONTAINED_MAX_ATTEMPTS` / `_SOURCE_LEAK_CORRECTION` are removed.
- **Kill switches for Extract skills and Draft from SOP (owner, 2026-09-29):** Extract skills (cron) gets "Stop extracting" beside its button (app header and Odoo form): a queued run is settled at once; a running one is flagged (`tag_extract_cancel_requested`) and the cron checks it the moment the reply lands, before anything is written, so the reply already paid for is not applied and the skills, rating scheme and knowledge profile stay as they were. Draft from SOP (runs inside its web request) gets "Stop" beside its button while drafting: the app frees the button and drops the reply; `POST /api/v1/task_templates/cancel_draft` stamps `template_draft_cancelled_at`, which refuses any further model call for a draft started before it (`vertex._check_cancelled`) and makes that request answer 409 `cancelled`. In both, the one call already on the wire finishes and is billed. New columns: needs `-u`.
- **Infra, not ours:** prod Postgres runs at 191-199 of 200 connections and the HPA can reach 5 pods (outage 11:43-11:53); the `etp-backend-etp-be` PodDisruptionBudget allows 1 of 2 pods down, so every node consolidation left one pod serving - raise `minAvailable` to 2 (drains then wait for a surge) or pause consolidation during exams.

## Part 7 - Audit findings register (2026-09-23)

From `finding-gaps.md`: 13 reviewers, **164 verified findings merged into 130 entries** (34 were the same issue found by two or more reviewers). **No blocker · 9 high · 36 medium · 72 low · 13 enhancement.** Three further claims were refuted outright and five partly refuted (§7.5). By role: senior software engineer 54, QA 23, product manager & UI/UX 45, audit 8. By area: backend 60, Flutter 27, Odoo UI 26, cross-cutting/ops 17.

### 7.1 Summary and fix-round outcome

- **Audit verdict then:** "Nothing found stops the push on its own, and all nine high findings have a small, contained fix - most are one condition or one string." Superseded 2026-09-23: round 1 found blockers B1-B5 in this wave (Part 1 §1.4.1).
- **Top 5 (audit, before the fix round):** (1) re-scoring an erased attempt grades the literal `[anonymized]` and overwrites the kept mark; (2) a labelling question keyed only by `ideal_labels` is paid for, always marks 0, and is not flagged keyless; (3) an auto-submitted placeholder is printed to the candidate as their own answer and marked "Incorrect" in red; (4) a failed re-grade or a spend-cap deferral writes its reason to the database and no screen anywhere reads it; (5) picking one question template silently inflates a paid run in Odoo and is refused outright in Flutter. All five fixed in the fix round (§7.2). Superseded 2026-09-23 as the top list: round 1 found blockers B1-B5.
- **"Implemented everything accurately" - mostly yes, with five known exceptions.** 71 of 87 plan items are done as written. 4 were built differently, 11 partially, 1 not at all. The exceptions that matter: W1's language guard does not cover the gateway sign-in routes; W6 added a `409 being_graded` refusal the plan had removed; W9's native JSON import still writes into the live bank; §6's "show candidates only new-instruction verdicts" mitigation was never built; and the 35-45 min throughput target models at 54-62 min because the pool formula yields 3 parallel calls per lane, not 4.
- **Money and marks are safe in the main paths.** Bulk grading, individual re-score, retries, fallback, kill, caching on and off, and parallel lanes were all driven end to end on throwaway databases with Vertex faked; marks were correct every time. The failures found are at the edges: erased attempts, one labelling key shape, malformed input, and a handful of cost leaks worth cents to a few dollars per run.
- **Weakest area is telling the operator what happened.** Eight medium findings are observability: cap refusals never log a WARNING, grading lines carry no candidate id under 4 parallel lanes, per-answer failures are never logged, and the cut-off check the deploy plan relies on cannot fire at the batch size prod will use.
- **Still needs a decision (6)** - Superseded 2026-09-23: all six settled by the owner (next bullet, Part 1 §1.2). As written then: native JSON import - drafts or exempt (already an open owner decision); keep or drop the 32k grading retry that went beyond the approved 16k floor; accept W6's new `409 being_graded` and amend the plan, or queue as decided; build the `llm_prompt_version` gate on old verdicts before the push, or accept the prod scan as the gate; whether a re-score that can move a released mark needs a confirmation (three surfaces disagree today); and whether client-drawn marker geometry on `image_label` is a hint leak or the server gate is over-strict (Finding L-2's owner).
- **Fix round (2026-09-23): all 9 high and all 36 medium findings fixed and merged**; backend 2,300/2,300, app 1,948 passed + 1 skipped. Each fix carries a test proven to fail on the pre-fix code, except where noted. Superseded 2026-09-23 in part: round 1 found pm-ux-candidate-3 (high) and pm-ux-admin-8, pm-ux-admin-13 only partly fixed, and pm-ux-candidate-12's fix regressed prod labelling (blocker B2).
- The six open decisions were settled by the owner and built (Part 1 §1.2): the cut-off retry asks for double the first ask up to the model's own limit and re-grades what still does not fit; the "being graded" refusal is kept and consistent on both paths; the native JSON bank export keeps restoring into the bank, with honest wording and an "are you sure"; the old-verdict gate is built behind `assessments_be_v2.verdict_requires_current_prompt` (default on); re-scoring a released mark asks first in the API and both UIs; marker geometry is gated exactly like the baked overlay (round 1: this broke prod labelling - blocker B2).
- **Correction:** `swe-api-models-1` does NOT reproduce on Odoo 19 - core's `_pre_dispatch` normalises the context language before any route body runs (instrumented run: `PROBE lang='en_US' best='en_GB'`). The prod incident it cites was the bearer path, which W1 fixed. What shipped is defence in depth for the `_authenticate` window, with a unit test that fails without it; the end-to-end test passes on old code too and says so. Treat it as low.
- **Status now:** 59 entries in §7.2 (one line each; the audit's full text in §7.7): 46 fixed, 4 partly fixed (swe-grading-12, pm-ux-candidate-3 - blocker B5, pm-ux-admin-8, pm-ux-admin-13), 1 regressed (pm-ux-candidate-12 - blocker B2), 5 resolved in docs, 2 settled by owner decision, 1 not a problem. 71 open (§7.3, full detail). The low and enhancement findings not touched by the fix round remain the backlog.
- How the entries read: grouped by reviewer role, then area, then severity; merged duplicates keep every id and sit under the role of the first id. **Severity is the verifier's final call** (raised or lowered notes say why). Verification: **confirmed** (a second pass reproduced it in code or at runtime), **uncertain** (the mechanism did not hold as described), **unverified** (no second pass ran).

### 7.3 Open backlog (full detail)

Low and enhancement findings not fixed in the fix round, in the audit's order (role, area, severity). Each keeps the audit's own text; a "Round 1" line adds what production validation found.

#### Senior software engineer - Backend

##### swe-grading-3, swe-logging-observability-10, qa-grading-edge-5 - The per-answer INFO line logs the judge's claimed score, not the mark actually stored
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:2073-2075` (also `1578-1582`, `1733-1749`)
- **What:** The line logs `_coerce_100(it.get("score"))` - the model's emitted number. The stored `llm_raw_100` may come from the image_label box mean, the deductions recompute or an integrity ceiling. Separately the `done: scored=%d/%d` line counts verdict-only image_ab answers in the numerator but not the denominator.
- **Evidence:** Probe printed `logged raw100=80.0 stored raw100=25.0 ceilings=[(verdict_contradiction, 25.0)]`; a live run logged `raw100=70.0` for a stored `53.33` and printed `done: scored=9/8`.
- **Impact:** Anyone using logs to answer "why did this candidate get 25" sees 80, and progress lines can read over 100%. It is also one INFO line per answer - roughly 12,000 per 704-candidate run.
- **Fix:** Log `resp.llm_raw_100` after the write (with the ceiling/recompute note), move per-answer detail to DEBUG, and count verdict-only answers in both halves.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### swe-grading-5 - A call that times out on our side leaves no ledger row and burns an attempt
**low** · confirmed · not reproduced · **open**
- **Where:** `services/vertex.py:210, 970, 982-1000, 1117`
- **What:** `_httpx().post` is unwrapped. `httpx.ReadTimeout` (read=180 s) propagates with no `_log_failed_call` and no `_log_usage`, although Vertex may still bill the generation. `_call_vertex`'s except clause catches only `VertexQuotaError`/`LLMRefusalError`, so the timeout gets no fallback and lands in the generic branch, which spends an attempt. With the new 16k floor a runaway single-answer call can generate far longer than the old 6,500-token limit allowed.
- **Evidence:** Only non-200 responses reach `_log_failed_call`; exceptions from the post skip every ledger write.
- **Impact:** Spend the daily and per-candidate caps cannot see; the LLM Budget screen under-reports.
- **Fix:** Catch httpx timeout/transport errors, write a failed-call ledger row noted `timeout`, and consider treating a timeout as a deferral rather than a spent attempt.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.
- **Round 1:** real and unfixed in the tree - no try/except for httpx timeouts (B1-34).

##### swe-grading-6, swe-scale-cost-2, qa-grading-edge-7, qa-backend-api-20 - The cache create rule counts answers, not calls, so a lone candidate pays for a cache used once
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1486-1506`
- **What:** `plan.queued[group]` sums every queued *answer* in the group across the paper. On a shared paper one candidate has one answer per question, so any group of 2+ questions always meets ">= 2". A bulk run holding a single candidate ("Score Failed Candidates (1)", a late submitter, the tail of a run) creates a Vertex cache that one call ever reads. In a parallel lane, concurrent jobs that lose the key lock also go inline while the winner creates.
- **Evidence:** Measured: group cache ~4,185 tokens; create + 15 min storage = $0.0131-$0.0156 against ~$0.010-0.012 inline for the same material; break-even is 1.74 calls. Reproduced with one queued candidate: creates=1, cached_calls=1.
- **Impact:** About $0.006 net loss plus one extra round trip per group per such run. Only reachable with the engineer switch `assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache = groups` (default off).
- **Fix:** Count distinct queued candidates (calls) per group, create only at 2 or more, and note it in the plan.
- **Verifier:** confirmed - but this is the approved rule verbatim (`final_implementation_plan.md:337` "Create rule: when >= 2 queued answers need the group"), so it is a design tweak, not a defect.
- **Round 1:** cannot happen on prod papers (no group reaches 4,096); on evals-* drafts at most ~$0.006 per group per run (B3-20).

##### swe-grading-7 - A successful cache create can go unbooked, and failed creates never reach the ledger
**low** · confirmed · not reproduced · **open**
- **Where:** `services/grading_cache.py:86-99, 129-170, 212-225`
- **What:** The booking for a create or refresh is written only after `_resolve` returns. If the row write or the own-cursor commit fails after Vertex answered 200, `resolve` swallows the exception and returns None: `_book` never runs, the input and storage cost never reaches the ledger or the daily cap, and the Vertex cache is orphaned for 15 minutes. Non-200 creates are not ledgered at all, unlike failed `generateContent` calls.
- **Evidence:** Read of the `resolve` / `_resolve` / `_create` ordering; the non-200 branch emits only a warning at `:148-152`.
- **Impact:** Rare under-reporting of cache spend; failed-create storms invisible on the LLM Budget screen.
- **Fix:** Book the create right after the 200, before the row write, and write a failed-call ledger row on create/extend refusals.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### swe-grading-9, qa-grading-edge-14 - A candidate at the per-candidate cap is re-picked every tick, for ever
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** (the re-score half) · **open**
- **Where:** `services/vertex.py:1418-1428`; `services/scoring.py:1914-1950`; `models/assessment.py:2955-2979`
- **What:** The $20 per-candidate cap sums the evaluator's lifetime spend with no time window, so it never resets. The refusal is a deferral (no attempt spent, answers stay pending, `scoring_requested` still set), so the shard re-selects the candidate every minute, commits `scoring`, builds the request, is refused and rewrites `llm_error`. A keyed re-score refused the same way keeps its key - and keyed candidates are dealt the tick limit *before* bulk work. The code comment claims the deferral clears "once the cap resets (UTC midnight)", which is true only of the daily cap.
- **Evidence:** Traced end to end; reproduced for the re-score case ("per-candidate-cap-at-run": key still set, mark kept, 0 calls, message "Waiting to be graded, no attempt used").
- **Impact:** Endless no-op work per tick, a misleading "waiting" message, and - with 20 such candidates on one shard - real starvation of bulk grading.
- **Fix:** Treat a per-candidate cap refusal as terminal for the run: park the candidate with the reason, clear `scoring_requested` and the key, and fix the comment.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; the cap genuinely has no time window.
- **Round 1:** the cap is lifetime and counts wasted calls (12610 spent $4.31 on 2 answers); unfixed (B1-25).

##### swe-grading-13 - `no_answer_key` ignores a scoring guide or penalties that are the only key
**low** · confirmed · not reproduced · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:861-863, 904-915, 1780-1781`
- **What:** `_KEY_FIELDS` leaves out `scoring_guide`, `penalties` and `decoys`. A prompt-writing question whose rubric JSON is a list, or a dict holding only a scoring guide, is *sent* that key but flagged `no_answer_key`, and Launch warns it has no key.
- **Evidence:** `_answer_key_dict` turns a non-dict rubric into `{"scoring_guide": raw}`, which `_image_prompt_key` forwards but `lacks_answer_key` does not count.
- **Impact:** False review flags and launch warnings on edge-shaped keys.
- **Fix:** Count `scoring_guide` and `penalties` as key fields for image_prompt/video_prompt.
- **Verifier:** confirmed but narrower: `_image_prompt_key` falls back to `ideal_prompt` -> `ideal_answer` -> `solution_json`, so the false flag needs both a guide-only rubric *and* an empty golden answer.
- **Round 1:** latent - 0 prod prompt questions keyed by a scoring guide alone (B3-09).

##### swe-api-models-2, qa-backend-api-11 - `/scoring` "queued" ignores individual re-scores and keeps counting finished candidates
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `controllers/api/admin.py:1769-1816`
- **What:** `queued` counts evaluators with `scoring_requested` regardless of `llm_state`. Individual re-scores set `rescore_request_key` on answers and never set `scoring_requested`, so with only re-scores waiting `queued=0` and `stalled=False` even if every grading cron is dead. After a run finishes, `scoring_requested` stays True on scored candidates, so `queued` stays at the cohort size.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: after a one-answer re-score, `/scoring` reported queued 0 while the phase summary said "1 queued"; after a finished bulk run, queued 3 with phase idle.
- **Impact:** The console's queue depth is wrong in both directions, and an admin's queued re-scores can wait for ever behind dead crons with no "grader not running" banner.
- **Fix:** Count keyed answers as queued (the partial index makes it cheap) and count only evaluators still in pending/scoring/partial/failed.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; the two surfaces genuinely disagree.
- **Round 1:** prod `/api/v1/scoring` returns queued=1,378 while nothing waits; #47's 53 stopped candidates appear in no lane (F4-25, B2-19).

##### swe-api-models-5, qa-backend-api-8 - Re-score is accepted on an archived paper, never graded, and lowers the archive's suspend flag
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:4977-5070, 2577, 2946, 2969`
- **What:** `action_rescore_individually` writes keys and calls `_withdraw_scoring_kill()` whatever the paper's `active` state, but both lane searches require `assessment_id.active = True`. The answer shows "Re-score queued" indefinitely, and lowering the flag undoes the stop `_suspend_scoring_for_archive` raised on calls already in flight.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: archived paper 24697, `POST /attempts/129973/rescore` returned 200 queued=1, the tick made 0 calls, detail read `phase=idle, summary='1 queued'`. After restoring the paper the next tick made the call.
- **Impact:** The admin is told "queued, usually within a minute" for work no lane can pick up, and the archive's stop is quietly lifted.
- **Fix:** Refuse with 409 `archived` (UserError in Odoo) before anything is written, or say the request is paused until the paper is restored.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### swe-api-models-7, qa-backend-api-7 - The post-launch question-count lock lives only in the API route
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `controllers/api/write.py:1047-1053`; `views/assessment_views.xml:184`
- **What:** W7's rule "the server refuses a CHANGED count on a launched assessment" is enforced in `assessment_update` and by the view's readonly only. `assessments.be.write()` accepts a changed `question_limit` on an in_progress paper from JSON-RPC, a list import, Studio or any internal write; the only model constraint checks `< 0`.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: admin `call_kw` write of `{question_limit: 2}` on launched paper 24701 returned True and read back 2 while the API returned 422 `locked_after_launch` for the same change. Candidate instructions read `question_limit`.
- **Impact:** Instructions and the paper can disagree. Low only because the Odoo form field is read-only.
- **Fix:** Move the check into `assessments.be.write` (same value passes) and let the route rely on it.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.
- **Round 1:** still route-only (`write.py:1047`); the deployed stepper is editable after launch and now gets 422 `locked_after_launch` (F4-11).

##### swe-api-models-10 - Late-add chatter can state the wrong question count
**low** · unverified · not reproduced · **open**
- **Where:** `controllers/api/admin.py:1102-1108`
- **What:** The audit line prints "provisioned with %d question(s) each" using `limit = min(question_limit, available)`, but candidates get the copied shared paper, whose length can differ (questions archived since launch, or an old per-person paper).
- **Evidence:** `_provision_late_candidates` sets `questions = list(shared)`, and `shared` is filtered by what is available.

##### swe-api-models-11, qa-backend-api-13 - The template archive sweep rewrites other generators silently and leaves a stale or newly-fixed count
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `models/task_template.py:272-299`
- **What:** Archiving a template edits `shape_quota_json` and `sop_question_count` on every generator that used it, with no chatter or log on those generators. The count is written only inside `if quotas:`, so when the last quota goes the old total stays; and a generator on auto (0) is rewritten to a fixed number by the first sweep.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced over the API: generator 33281 with `{5341:3, 5342:2}` and count 0. Archive 5341 -> quotas `{5342:2}`, count 2. Archive 5342 -> quotas `{}`, count stays 2.
- **Impact:** A generator's next run asks for a size nobody chose, with no trail an admin can find. The Flutter sweep keeps the count too, so this is parity, not a regression.
- **Fix:** Post a chatter line on each changed generator; keep auto (0) as 0 and decide the count explicitly when the last quota goes, in both Odoo and the app.
- **Verifier:** confirmed exactly as described.

##### swe-logging-observability-5 - Individual re-scores and Kill cannot be followed end to end in logs
**low** · confirmed · not reproduced · **open**
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:5045-5057, 2491-2557, 4772`; `services/scoring.py:1584-1586, 1817`
- **What:** A re-score writes only a chatter line: no server log, no `ETP_AUDIT` event, and the uuid4 request key is never logged (the ledger note is just `rescore(n)`). A kill - button or route - is not logged at all, nor is a re-score click that lowers the kill flag. A failed re-grade's reason lives only in `evaluator.llm_error`, which `_llm_score_start` clears the next time that candidate is graded.
- **Evidence:** The only `audit.emit('scoring…')` in the addon is `scoring.enqueue`; grep finds no logger or audit call carrying `rescore_request_key` or `kill`.
- **Impact:** When an admin says "I clicked re-score and nothing changed" or "kill didn't stop it", Loki cannot show request -> call -> outcome.
- **Fix:** Emit `scoring.rescore` and `scoring.kill` audit events, put `key[:8]` in the begin log and the ledger note, and log each key's outcome including "kept previous mark: <reason>".
- **Verifier:** confirmed, but lowered from medium: chatter, `llm_error` and the scoring console are the designed trail - this is a Loki-only gap.

##### swe-logging-observability-8, swe-scale-cost-3 - Cache lines carry no key or model, and several fallbacks to uncached grading log nothing
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** (the group-minimum half) · **open**
- **Where:** `services/grading_cache.py:104-116, 148-152, 182-190, 222-225`; `services/scoring.py:1457-1478, 1534-1538`
- **What:** "cache create refused" and "create failed" omit the key and model, although a failure starts a 10-minute window in which that key is graded inline with no further log. These fall back to inline with no line at all: a 404 on extend, a lost lock, an API-key setup, a model with no `cache_min`, a group under the minimum size, and per-person papers. A group whose instructions plus material fall under the model minimum is skipped silently.
- **Evidence:** Dry run on the 750-candidate fixture: batch 20 gives one group at ~4,185 tokens (just over the 4,096 minimum, a 2% margin); batch 8 gives 3,394 and 2,542 tokens, always inline - and the local database runs at batch 8. `_book`'s ERROR omits `exc_info` and the estimated dollars.
- **Impact:** An engineer who turns `scoring_cache=groups` on and sees no savings cannot tell from logs why, or which key failed.
- **Fix:** Put `key[:12]`, model and location on every cache line; log once per paper when a group is under the minimum; include `exc_info` and the estimate in `_book`'s error.
- **Verifier:** confirmed. Minor overstatement: a commit failure after a billed create *is* logged by `resolve()` with `key[:12]` and `exc_info` - just not as a cost error.

##### swe-logging-observability-9 - A lane failure after calls were billed does not log how many paid results were thrown away
**low** · confirmed · not reproduced · **open**
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:2868-2916`
- **What:** `_auto_score_failed` logs only "Auto-score failed for evaluator %s" with a traceback. `_auto_score_finish` never passes `run`, so `len(run.pending)` and the assessment id are lost.
- **Evidence:** The team's key incident metric ("calls thrown away") had to be reconstructed by joining against the ledger.
- **Impact:** If a SerializationFailure or pool issue returns, its cost cannot be read from logs.
- **Fix:** Pass `run` into `_auto_score_failed` and log `billed_calls_discarded=%d asmt=%s`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed. Imprecision: `pool.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=True)` lets in-flight calls finish, so it is the un-stored (not dropped) count that goes unlogged.
- **Round 1:** unfixed; prod's 3,800 discarded paid calls ($190.77) are visible only through a ledger join - log `billed_calls_discarded` and alert on it (B1-27).

##### swe-logging-observability-11 - The language-fallback fix logs neither the offending code nor how many requests it rescued
**low** · confirmed · not reproduced · **open**
- **Where:** `models/ir_http.py:722-730`
- **What:** The guard logs `_logger.exception("ETP: could not validate the request language")` with no `%r` of the language code and no route, and a successful fallback (en_GB -> en_US) logs nothing.
- **Evidence:** Read of the new block; only the exception path logs.
- **Impact:** The plan's 24 h check ("no Invalid language code") can only show absence, never that the guard is doing work.
- **Fix:** Include the code in the message, and log once per (process, code) at INFO when a fallback is applied.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### swe-scale-cost-6 - After a bulk re-queue, the outlier recompute hits SerializationFailure against the lanes
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:3662-3683, 944-982`
- **What:** Re-queued candidates drop out of the cohort, so their `score_outlier=True` flips to False - on rows the lanes write at mark-scoring and finish time. The recompute excludes nothing a lane holds.
- **Evidence:** 4-lane stress run: 795 candidates re-queued, recompute every 2 s. 8 of 39 passes died, each logging an `odoo.sql_db` ERROR "could not serialize access due to concurrent update" with a ~100-row VALUES dump plus an ERROR traceback. The lanes lost 0 of 795.
- **Impact:** The deploy checklist's 24 h watch ("no SerializationFailure from grading") will find this text at ERROR after any "Re-score This Assessment" on a paper with flagged candidates. Log noise only on the recompute side.
- **Fix:** Leave rows with `llm_state='scoring'` or `subjective_pending > 0` out of the flip write; log the collision at WARNING under `mute_logger('odoo.sql_db')`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed, including that the cron's own handler concedes it cannot unwind a serialization failure.
- **Round 1:** logs only; check Loki after the first post-deploy bulk re-score. The recompute cron was prod's main collider at HEAD (B1-35, B1-04).

##### swe-scale-cost-8 - One failed call turns into 15-20 single-answer calls (pre-existing)
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1594-1598, 1953-1954`
- **What:** When a whole call fails (5xx, timeout, unparseable reply), every one of its 15-20 answers is marked failed with `attempts=1`. The next tick grades each of them in its own call, each resending the ~1,744-token instructions.
- **Evidence:** A stress run over answers already at `llm_attempts=1` produced 2,562 ledger rows for ~160 candidates - about 16 calls per candidate instead of 1, roughly 40k input tokens against ~5k. Baseline has the identical line, so this is not new.
- **Impact:** A Vertex error burst multiplies calls and cost 15-20x for the affected candidates and can stall the run. Bounded by `llm_max_attempts=3` and the spend caps, so wall-clock is the sharper cost.
- **Fix:** On a whole-call failure, retry the batch once as a batch (or split it in half) before falling back to one call per answer.
- **Verifier:** confirmed, both halves.
- **Round 1:** small on prod - 155 single-answer retry calls (3%) on 2-answer papers (B1-32).

##### swe-grading-10 - Cached input booked at 10% for Gemini 2.0 rows the catalog marks cacheable
**enhancement** · confirmed · not reproduced · **open**

- **What:** `CACHED_INPUT_SHARE = 0.10` is applied to every row via `price.get("cached_in", rate_in * CACHED_INPUT_SHARE)`. The code's own comment limits the 90% discount to Gemini 2.5+, but the `gemini-2.0-flash(-lite)` rows carry `cache_min: 2048`. Google prices 2.0 cached input at about 25%.

- **Verifier:** confirmed but fully dormant - the binding rule forbids a model change and the cache is only reachable on the configured scoring model, hence enhancement.

- **Fix:** Pause while hidden, resume on `visibilitychange`, and use one batched read per list.

#### Senior software engineer - Flutter

##### swe-flutter-5 - The answer-page re-score watch has no hidden-tab pause and re-reads every tick when idle or stalled
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `lib/assessment/screens/admin/response_detail_screen.dart:53-127`
- **What:** `moved = numbers != _lastNumbers || !(pipe?.phase?.isBusy ?? false)`, so any non-busy phase - idle, stalled, an archived paper - counts as movement and the full answer is re-read every tick. It runs up to 360 ticks (1 hour) with no `WidgetsBindingObserver` and no backoff, missing W4.4's "pause hidden tabs".
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: with the answer queued and `/scoring` returning `stalled`, 60 simulated seconds produced 6 `/scoring` and 6 `/responses/90/205` requests. `ScoringPhase.isBusy`'s own doc says a watch on stalled must not keep polling.
- **Impact:** ~720 requests an hour per open answer tab on a stalled or archived queue, continuing in background tabs.
- **Fix:** Reuse the assessment page's hidden-tab observer and backoff; stop (or drop to one read a minute) on stalled/idle after one confirming re-read.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; the code's own comment admits there is no hidden-tab sleep.
- **Round 1:** 6 `/scoring` calls a minute visible and hidden; code comment admits no hidden-tab sleep (F1-14).

- **Impact:** The cost and speed promised to the operator are wrong until and unless the setting is changed.

##### swe-scale-cost-4 - The detail-screen scoring poll never backs off while a run is active
**low** · confirmed · not reproduced · **open**
- **Where:** `lib/assessment/screens/admin/assessment_detail_screen.dart:119-123, 346-349`
- **What:** The backoff fingerprint includes `pipe.summary` ("N queued · M scoring · K scored"), which the server recomputes on every candidate commit - and lanes commit one candidate at a time. So nearly every 5 s tick sees a change and the 15/30 s rungs never engage.
- **Evidence:** At 12-16 candidates a minute, the chance two polls 5 s apart see the same numbers is about 0.29; in the stress runs the counts moved on every poll. The route itself is cheap: 13 queries, 34 ms, 207 req/s at 10 clients.
- **Impact:** About 10-11 requests a minute per open tab for the whole run against the plan's ~4, and it drives the 60-minute watch cap in `swe-scale-cost-1`.
- **Fix:** Round the counts in the fingerprint (`queued` also changes per candidate, so dropping `summary` alone does not fix it) and snap back to 5 s only on a phase change.
- **Verifier:** confirmed, with that correction to the proposed fix.
- **Round 1:** during a real run the backoff never engages (11 vs 12 calls/min) (F1-10, B1-31).

##### qa-backend-api-10 - Each re-score/queue click rewrites the shared paper row, so concurrent clicks log serialization ERRORs
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:1457-1473` (`_remember_scoring_tally`), called from `action_rescore_individually:5046`, `action_queue_llm_score:4903`, `action_llm_score_all:2410`
- **What:** W2 removed lane writes to the cohort row, but every idle-paper click still writes `scoring_last_*` on it with no comparison against the current values. Parallel clicks on one paper collide; Odoo retries, but each retry logs at ERROR. The same row is written by the recompute cron.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: 8 concurrent `POST /attempts/129975/rescore` all returned 200 and the server log took 7 "could not serialize access due to concurrent update" ERRORs on `UPDATE assessments_be SET scoring_last_candidates...`.
- **Impact:** Log noise that clashes with the deploy check "no SerializationFailure for 24 h", plus a small collision window with the recompute cron.
- **Fix:** Write the tally only when a value actually changes.

##### qa-backend-api-12 - A re-score key on an answer that no longer needs the grader is never cleared
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** (artificially) · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1561-1569` (`begin_evaluator`); `models/assessment.py:2946`
- **What:** `begin_evaluator` builds `chosen` as `needs_llm and rescore_request_key` and returns without clearing keys on the rest, while the shard's keyed search tests only `rescore_request_key != False`. If a keyed answer stops needing the grader (the question type is changed after the click), the key stays for ever: the candidate is picked first on every tick and the paper reads "queued".
- **Evidence:** A key set by SQL on MCQ answer 44662 survived 2 ticks and the summary kept "1 queued". Not reproduced through the UI.
- **Impact:** Edge case, but the work never ends and eats tick budget; 20 such rows would take a shard's whole tick limit.
- **Fix:** In `begin_evaluator`, clear keys on keyed answers that are not `needs_llm`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### qa-backend-api-14 - `question_ids` with an out-of-range number gives a 500
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `controllers/api/common.py:458-462`
- **What:** `id_list_arg` catches only `TypeError`/`ValueError`. `json` parses `1e400` to `float('inf')` and `int(inf)` raises `OverflowError`, which reaches the generic handler.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced on `/attempts/129972/rescore` and `/assessments/24701/update` with `{"question_ids":[1e400]}` -> 500 `server_error`. A fuzz of 13 routes x 12 malformed bodies found no other 5xx.

- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### qa-backend-api-17 - (Predates this build) The results export denominator disagrees with the paper total on force-submitted attempts
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/export.py:182, 242, 335`
- **What:** `total_max` sums `max_possible_score + llm_max_score`, which count only submitted / needs_llm responses, while the app and `score_percent` divide by `_paper_component_totals` over the whole drawn question order. Unanswered written questions add no subjective max.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: candidate 129974 sat a 6-question paper and answered 1 with force submit; the CSV shows `total_score 0, total_max 3` while the attempt has `raw_max 6`. No patch in this build touches `export.py`.

##### qa-backend-api-18 - (Predates this build) A repeated submit returns 409 `attempt_locked`, so the documented "already" reply never happens
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `controllers/api/candidate.py:505, 688-690`
- **What:** `_write_guard` refuses a locked attempt before `exam_submit`'s `already: True` branch can run, and submit sets `is_locked=True` together with `state='submitted'`, so that branch is unreachable for a normal double-tap.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: a second `POST /exam/<token>/submit` returned 409 `{code: attempt_locked}`.
- **Impact:** A client retrying submit on a flaky network sees an error after a success.
- **Fix:** Let `exam_submit` answer `ok({submitted: true, already: true})` for a locked attempt of the assigned candidate.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### qa-grading-edge-4 - NaN or Infinity in a reply score becomes 100/100
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1045-1065, 1087-1095, 1239`
- **What:** Python's `json.loads` accepts `NaN` and `Infinity`. `_num_or_none(nan)` returns `nan` (not False), so the no-usable-score guard does not fire, and `_coerce_100(nan)` returns 100.0 because `min(100.0, nan)` is 100.0. The same applies to `box_scores` values and deduction points.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: `{"score":NaN,"deductions":[]}` stored 100.0; a NaN re-grade replaced a 40 with 100; a NaN box scored 100. Unit run on the real helper: `_coerce_100(nan)`, `(inf)`, `('Infinity')`, `('NaN')` all return 100.0.
- **Impact:** A malformed or manipulated reply gives a perfect mark instead of an error. Unlikely from Gemini's JSON mode, but it is a money/marks path with no guard.
- **Fix:** Reject non-finite values in `_coerce_100`/`_num_or_none`, and parse replies with a `parse_constant` that raises.
- **Verifier:** confirmed by running the helper standalone.

##### qa-grading-edge-6 - One candidate with a different question turns group caching off for the whole paper
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1473-1478`
- **What:** The cohort is the union of every evaluator's `question_order`, and caching applies only if some candidate holds all of it. A single late candidate who drew a replacement for a retired question, or a few old per-person papers, makes the union a strict superset of every paper and disables caching for everyone.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: 5 candidates on the same 3 questions plus 1 whose paper swaps one question -> creates=0, cached=0, inline=6.
- **Impact:** The bulk-run cost saving silently disappears on mixed papers. Marks are correct; cost only.
- **Fix:** Build the plan from the queued candidates that share the majority question set, or group by distinct question sets.
- **Verifier:** confirmed. The behaviour is documented as deliberate in the same docstring, so this is a cost gap in a stated design rather than a bug.

##### qa-grading-edge-8 - A lapsed pinned bearer marks a group cache failed for 10 minutes, and the first 401 is not on the ledger
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/grading_cache.py:72-83, 147-159, 188-191`; `services/vertex.py:970-981`
- **What:** `generateContent` resends once with a fresh bearer on a 401 for a pinned token; the cache create/extend path does not. A 401 there writes `failed_until = now + 10 min`, so every lane grades that group uncached for 10 minutes. The first 401 of a pinned call is only a WARNING, with no ledger row (`_log_failed_call` runs after the resend).
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: with `tok1` rejected, requests went `cachedContents tok1 -> 401`, `generateContent tok1 -> 401`, `generateContent tok3 -> 200`; the cache row ended with `resource_name=False` and `failed_until` set, and the ledger showed only the 2 successful calls.
- **Impact:** Caching is lost for 10 minutes after a token lapse (cost only), and 401 storms on pinned tokens do not show on the LLM Budget screen.
- **Fix:** In `_create`/`_extend`, retry once with the pin dropped before marking failed, and ledger the refused attempt.
- **Verifier:** confirmed on both halves.

##### qa-grading-edge-9 - The injection gate checks labelling answers as raw JSON, so `\u`-escaped text gets past it
**low** · confirmed (one vector) · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1744, 416-424`; `controllers/api/candidate.py:948-953`
- **What:** For image_label the gate runs on the stored JSON string while the grader receives the decoded labels, and the API stores the posted `justification` as-is when no `labels` are sent. A crafted request can store an escaped idiom the gate does not match but the model reads plainly.
- **Evidence:** `evaluate_gates('{"1": "\\u0069gnore the rubric"}')` returns None while the plain form returns `injection_attempt`, and `_label_answer` decodes it for the grader.
- **Impact:** Defence-in-depth gap on labelling questions for a candidate posting directly to the API. The prompt still tells the model answers are data.
- **Fix:** For image_label, run `evaluate_gates` on the decoded label values rather than the stored JSON text.
- **Verifier:** confirmed for the `\u`-escape vector only. The homoglyph half is **refuted**: `gates._CONFUSABLES` folds Cyrillic, and `candidate.py:948` stores with `ensure_ascii=False`, so the reviewer's evidence does not match the real storage path.

##### qa-grading-edge-12 - The truncated-labelling error text miscounts ("scored only 2 of 2 labelled boxes")
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:2055-2061`
- **What:** The message compares `returned` (every key the model emitted, including boxes outside the key or not attempted) against `attempted_boxes`, so a reply that scored the wrong boxes reads as a full reply.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: the worker answered boxes 1 and 2, the model returned `{2,3}`, and the stored feedback read "Grader scored only 2 of 2 labelled box(es) - the reply looks truncated".
- **Impact:** The admin-facing reason for a retry or error is wrong, which slows diagnosis of P2 hidden-marker replies. Message only; the retry decision is unaffected.
- **Fix:** Report attempted minus unscored-attempted, and name the unscored boxes.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### qa-grading-edge-13 - Credential failures (401 unpinned, 403) use up attempts and push the cohort to error
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/vertex.py:998`; `services/scoring.py:1939-1955`
- **What:** A 429, the rate ceiling, the spend caps and a full DB pool are deferred with no attempt used. A 401 without a pin (direct access token, revoked service-account key) or a 403 raises a plain `RuntimeError`, which `_store_submission` treats like a broken reply: each tick spends an attempt, and after 3 every answer is `error` with 0.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced ("401-unpinned"): state failed, attempts 1, feedback "Vertex error [401]: UNAUTHENTICATED". The 403 path is identical. Pre-existing.
- **Impact:** A credential outage during a bulk run parks the whole cohort in `error` (0 marks) until someone runs Retry Failed.
- **Fix:** Treat 401/403 like a quota refusal - no attempt used, reason in `llm_error` - once the pinned-token resend has been tried.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; recoverable by Retry Failed, which is why it stays low despite the cohort-wide blast radius.

##### qa-grading-edge-15 - The cache ledger test depends on a database with no existing cache rows
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `tests/test_a_bulk_run_caches_questions_never_answers.py:191-192, 486-494`
- **What:** `test_create_and_refresh_are_on_the_ledger_with_no_candidate` unpacks exactly one `scoring_cache_create` row from an unscoped search, and `_row()` is `search([], limit=1)`. It errors on any database where caching has ever run: a calibration copy, staging after the push, or a dev database.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: 235 targeted grading tests on a throwaway database after harness runs gave "0 failed, 1 error" with `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)` at line 494. Every other grading/cache/re-score/parallel/kill test passed.
- **Impact:** A false red on the pre-push suite run against a realistic database copy, which invites people to ignore failures.
- **Fix:** Scope `_ledger`/`_row` to rows created in the test (id greater than the max taken in `setUp`).
- **Verifier:** confirmed. Blast radius is small today: `etp_local` has no `assessments_be_scoring_cache` table and the switch ships off.

##### qa-grading-edge-11 - Labelling answers that cannot earn a mark still pay for a Vertex call
**enhancement** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1715-1752, 670-672, 720-729`
- **What:** Two cases are sent to the grader although the mark is fixed at 0: image_label with no key at all (flagged `no_answer_key`, total = 0) and a label map whose every value is blank or a single character (no box counts as attempted). `_prepare_submission` short-circuits only image_ab verdict-only, AB key drift and gate hits.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: "keyless-label" -> flags `['no_answer_key']`, raw 88.0, `llm_score 0/1`; `{"1":"","2":" ","3":"x"}` -> the gate returns None, calls=1, attempted_boxes 0, scored 0.
- **Impact:** Wasted spend, plus a confusing "raw 88 but failed" display on keyless labelling.
- **Fix:** Short-circuit image_label with no boxes or zero attempted boxes to a stored 0, as verdict-only and gated answers already are.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### qa-flutter-ui-1 - A launched assessment's header reports the generator pool, contradicting the now-locked Questions field
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**

- **What:** fe-polish locked the Configuration "Questions" field after launch and changed it to `questionLimit > 0 ? questionLimit : effectiveQuestionCount`. The page header subtitle was left on `effectiveQuestionCount`, the generator's in-use pool count, so on any launched paper whose `question_limit` is below the pool size one screen states two different question counts - and the bigger one is wrong.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced live twice. Assessment 24701 launched from a 10-question generator with `question_limit=3` shows header "… · 10 questions", Configuration "QUESTIONS 3", history "3 question(s) each". A candidate's review screen for a comparable paper read "3 of 3 answered".
- **Impact:** An admin reading the main summary line believes the cohort answered 10 questions when they answered 3. Nothing downstream uses the number.
- **Fix:** After launch, drive the header subtitle from the same `questionLimit or effectiveQuestionCount` value the Configuration field uses.

##### qa-flutter-ui-3 - "Re-score N selected" counts ticked rows it will not grade
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `lib/assessment/screens/admin/responses_screen.dart:506, 716` vs `_rescoreSelected` at `:418-431`

When the selection mixes both, the label and the toast disagree and nothing says which rows were skipped. The all-objective case is handled; the mixed case is not.

- **Impact:** Cosmetic - the spend is correct and the toast states the real number - but an operator checking a bulk re-score sees 2 promised and 1 queued.

- **Round 1:** still counts every tick; new tooltip "Grades exactly the ticked answers." is false when an MCQ is ticked (F1-19).

- **What:** The "already sent" banner ("Editing it here changes the form only … Send it again to publish a new pool from these edits") is gated on `record.data.published` alone, ignoring `props.readonly`, while the same wave made the Odoo form `edit="0"` with the structure field `readonly="1"`. #### Audit - Cross-cutting / Ops

##### apc-11 - The Settings help for "Parallel Calls in Use" describes a formula that gives the wrong number
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · **open**
- **Where:** `models/res_config_settings.py:327-329`
- **What:** The help reads "the setting, lowered to fit half of the database pool (db_maxconn), less 2 connections for each shard's own cursor, at 2 connections per call." It omits that the half-pool is split across the shards, so worked through as written on a pool of 64 it gives 12-15, not the 3 the code produces and the deploy note promises.
- **Evidence:** The code is `room = max(1, (pool // 2 - 2 * shards) // (2 * shards))`; verified at runtime, `db_maxconn` 64 + 4 shards -> 3, and 80 -> 4. The plan states the correct numbers.
- **Impact:** An ops reader sizing `db_maxconn` from this help reaches the wrong conclusion about what raising the setting costs.
- **Fix:** Rewrite as "half the pool, shared across the shards: each shard gets (db_maxconn/2)/shards connections, less 2 for its own cursor, at 2 per call."
- **Verifier:** confirmed (the reviewer's arithmetic differs slightly from mine - 15 vs 12 - but the conclusion is the same: the help cannot yield the promised 3).

### 7.4 Plan conformance

The audit's plan-conformance table (71 of 87 items done as written; the 16 exceptions) and what happened since: Part 2 §2.20.

### 7.5 Refuted / not an issue

- **apc-1** - "the backend suite is red in the push candidate". Not reproducible: a fresh `audit_base_7` copy ran "0 failed, 0 error(s) of 2133 tests", and the named cache test passed 7/7 runs alone. The observed red looks like load contention, not a code defect.
- **apc-2** - "W15's baseline calibration arm cannot run on the baseline checkout". The baseline arm runs fine on the actual pre-build lane (`etp-lanes/be-baseline`), whose prompt hashes to the runbook's `bundled:34c42d2f`; what is left is an unfriendly `AttributeError` instead of a clean `SystemExit` on a git-HEAD lane.
- **apc-7** - "deploy notes never mention that `api_auth_gateway` ships in the same push". It is documented twice, in the plan's scope line and in CHANGE_SUMMARY; only §6's checklist omits the cross-reference.
- **qa-flutter-ui-1 (badge half)** - the "Selected Questions" badge is *not* wrong: it counts the ticked rows its own tab lists. Only the header subtitle is.
- **qa-grading-edge-9 (homoglyph half)** - Cyrillic homoglyphs *are* caught by the gate's confusable folding, and the API stores labels with `ensure_ascii=False`. Only the `\u`-escape vector survives.
- **swe-grading-4 (two sub-claims)** - the C-2 retry comment *was* updated, and the `_grade_job` re-ask loop is pre-existing, so "4 paid calls instead of 2" holds only for mid-size batches.
- **qa-backend-api-6 (mechanism)** - the "two threads share one cursor" explanation does not hold under the test runner; the flake is real but undiagnosed.
- **qa-backend-api-4 (one sub-claim)** - the payload import's "title is ignored" complaint is weak: `title` is not a key of the documented `question_bank` shape.

### 7.6 Coverage and limits of the audit

**A dedicated QA pass driving the Odoo admin UI in a browser was NOT part of this audit. That agent stalled and was dropped.** The Odoo admin UI is covered here by code review (the `swe-odoo-ui` and `pm-ux-admin` reviewers, the latter of which did walk ~20 screens in headless Chromium and exercised the import, re-score, quota, kill and publish flows), and by the earlier headless-browser review run during the build itself. There is no systematic, adversarial click-through of the Odoo console in this report, so Odoo-side findings should be read as "found by reading the code and spot-checking the screen", not as "the screen was tested".

What was run, by whom:

- **Backend and grading code review** (`swe-grading`, `swe-api-models`, `swe-logging-observability`) - read-only. No database, no server, no Vertex call. Everything diffed against the pre-build lane to separate new behaviour from pre-existing. `swe-api-models`' findings are all unverified (no second pass ran on that lane).
- **Odoo UI** (`swe-odoo-ui`) - read-only against the Odoo 19 web client source, plus the build's own screenshots. No browser run of its own and no JS test runner, so none of its findings is reproduced.
- **Flutter** (`swe-flutter`) - full analyze (clean) and test run (1,906 passed, 1 skipped) in a scratch copy, plus 4 throwaway tests that reproduced findings 1, 2, 3 and 5. No running backend, no browser.
- **Scale and cost** (`swe-scale-cost`) - a 750-candidate fixture on a throwaway database with Vertex faked at the HTTP layer: route query counts and latency, a 4-lane stress run (795/795 graded, 0 wasted calls, peak 22 connections), a token dry run baseline-vs-new (instructions 4,550 -> ~1,744 tokens; 47 real calls -62%), and Playwright measurement of the Odoo badge polling. Not verified: prod server mode and `db_maxconn`, real Gemini token counts (chars/4 was used), real Vertex latency.
- **API and flow QA** (`qa-backend-api`) - a throwaway database driven over real HTTP with bearer tokens and Vertex faked in-process: the full suite, 13 Accept-Language sign-ins, launch and late-add, the exam lifecycle, bulk and individual scoring with every refusal path, release, exports, Form Studio publish, four import formats, task templates, settings, cache on and off, and a 13-route x 12-body malformed fuzz. Not covered: Odoo screens, Flutter, real cron threads, the pool-full deferral, and real Vertex billing behaviour.
- **Grading edge cases** (`qa-grading-edge`) - a throwaway database driven through the real cron entry point with a scripted fake Vertex, every scenario run serially and at 4 parallel calls: all question types, malformed and hostile replies, model failures and fallback, re-grades, caching (create, hit, 404, failed create, extend, lock loss), kill mid-run, and two lanes plus the outlier cron concurrently (12/12 scored, 0 serialization failures). Not covered: real Vertex wording, UI rendering, prod topology, mark calibration.
- **Flutter UI QA** (`qa-flutter-ui`) - the built web bundle served against a throwaway Odoo instance and driven with headless Chromium (en-GB locale, all scoring crons disabled, Vertex never called). Verified live: chips and counts, every re-score payload, the launch warning, the post-launch count lock, IST on every timestamp, the released candidate answer sheet, email paging, and polling backoff plus hidden-tab pause. Not exercised: the lowered "in use per lane" branch, the price/capability warning, the multi-candidate toast, and a fresh end-to-end sitting.
- **Admin product review** (`pm-ux-admin`) - headless Chromium over an Odoo instance with outbound sockets blocked and Draft-from-SOP faked; Flutter compared by source only, so no rendered-pixel, contrast, focus-order or screen-reader check on the console. Form Studio publish could not be completed in the browser (S3 media fetch blocked) and was verified through the ORM instead.
- **Candidate product review** (`pm-ux-candidate`) - read-only, plus a full Flutter test run (1,938 passed, 1 skipped) and 4 probe tests against the real parsers. No database, no server, no browser: nothing was confirmed by rendering. The mobile-width finding comes from layout code only - no RenderFlex overflow was measured. Proctoring behaviour is browser-only and was read, not exercised.
- **Plan conformance** (`audit-plan-conformance`) - every W-item and §1/§6 rule checked against the code with file:line evidence, the full backend suite run on a fresh copy, runtime measurement of effective parallel calls, the settings readback, the cache-switch default and the prompt fingerprint, plus a module downgrade/rollback exercise. Could not check anything on production: the installed manifest version, the stored settings (400/20/60, shards 4, tick 5), `db_maxconn`, or whether any prod answer carries an old prompt version - so W15's real verdict and the `apc-3` exposure remain unquantified.

Across every reviewer: all scratch databases were dropped and all servers stopped. The audit stated that no production system was touched; superseded 2026-09-23: one audit subagent did authenticate against production without authorisation and was stopped (Part 5 §5.6.2).
