##### swe-flutter-1, pm-ux-admin-6 - A failed re-grade or a capped deferral writes its reason to the database and no screen reads it
**high** · confirmed · **reproduced** (widget test) · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1398-1410, 1890-1904` (writer); `controllers/api/serializers.py:1476` (`subjective.error`); `lib/assessment/domain/models.dart:5224-5261` (parser); no Odoo view references `llm_error`
- **What:** When a queued re-score of a scored answer fails, the backend keeps the old mark, clears the key and writes the reason on the candidate as `evaluator.llm_error`. W3.1 uses the same field for "Waiting to be graded, no attempt used: <429 / spend cap>". `Attempt.fromJson` parses `subjective.score/max/pending/state/scoring_requested/has_terminal_error` and never `error`, and `llm_error` appears in no Odoo form, roster or All Attempts column. So the answer page just turns "Re-score queued" back into "Re-score" with the old mark and no message.
- **Evidence:** Widget test mounting `AttemptDetailScreen` with `subjective.error='Re-score of Q205 failed, its previous mark was kept: no score'` finds that text 0 times. `grep -rn llm_error views/` is empty; a marker written onto attempt 1090 appeared on none of three live Odoo screens.
- **Impact:** Plan W6 says "on failure or refusal the old mark stays and the reason is shown". The admin can read a silent failure as the re-grade confirming the mark, and the exact case this build added telemetry for - a queue waiting on money or capacity rather than broken - presents as a silent "Pending".
- **Fix:** Parse `subjective.error` into `Attempt` and show it as a Notice on the candidate and answer pages; add `llm_error` to the Odoo attempt form and as an optional roster column.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; the reason is written and sent but rendered nowhere, on either console.

##### qa-backend-api-1 - Re-scoring an erased (PII-anonymised) attempt grades the `[anonymized]` placeholder and overwrites the kept mark
**high** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:4977` (no `pii_anonymized` guard), `4552` (`_anonymize_pii`); `controllers/api/admin.py:1668`
- **What:** Erasure keeps the justification as the non-empty tag `[anonymized]` so `needs_llm` stays True, and the old mark is supposed to be kept. This build now lets an admin re-score an answer that already has a mark, and neither the route nor the model refuses an erased attempt - so the grader is paid to mark the literal string `[anonymized]` and its result replaces the kept mark.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced on a throwaway database with Vertex faked. Attempt 129977, answer 44672 scored 75 with `final_mark 1`. `POST /attempts/129977/erase` -> 200; `POST /attempts/129977/rescore {question_ids:[42571]}` -> 200 `queued=1`. Next tick, the fake Vertex received `{"id":44672,...,"answer":"[anonymized]"}` and the answer was stored `llm_raw_100=5, final_mark=0`. Flutter's `canRescore` has no `piiAnonymized` check either, so the button is live on an erased attempt.
- **Impact:** The erase promise "Numeric scores and pass/fail were kept" is broken, a paid call is wasted, and a candidate's result can flip. It reaches every attempt the PII retention cron has anonymised.
- **Fix:** Refuse re-score and requeue on `pii_anonymized` attempts (409 `erased`), or skip answers whose justification is the anonymised tag, in both `action_rescore_individually` and `action_reset_failed_scoring`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; every link in the chain checks out in code as well as at runtime.

##### qa-grading-edge-1 - A labelling question keyed only by `ideal_labels` is paid for, always marks 0, and is not flagged keyless
**high** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:361` (`_label_total_boxes`), `806-829` (`_label_boxes`), `904-915` (`lacks_answer_key`); `models/assessment.py:5869`; `controllers/api/candidate.py:854-869`
- **What:** `_label_boxes` sends the model the `ideal_labels` boxes - its docstring claims the same sources as `_label_total_boxes`, which is false: the total counts only the behavioural key or detections. So `total = 0`, `_apply_image_label_boxes` returns the reply untouched, box scores are stored unfiltered, and `_label_marks` returns 0 for every candidate. `lacks_answer_key()` says the question has a key, so Launch shows no warning and no `no_answer_key` flag is set. The candidate still sees one input per box via the `ideal_labels_count` fallback.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced with Vertex faked: `lacks_answer_key=False`, total boxes 0, boxes sent `{'1','2'}`; after grading, state `scored`, raw 95.0, `label_box_scores_json={"1":95,"2":95,"7":100}`, `llm_score 0/1`, flags False. The mark logic is unchanged from baseline; `lacks_answer_key` and the launch warning are new in this build and miss this shape.
- **Impact:** Every candidate silently gets 0 on such a question while a Vertex call is billed for each answer, with no launch warning and no flag pointing at the cause.
- **Fix:** Count `ideal_labels` boxes in `_label_total_boxes` (the same sources `_label_boxes` uses), or treat these questions as keyless: warn at Launch and flag `no_answer_key`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed, and reachability is worse than reported - neither launch gate filters on the new `has_valid_key` and `_keyless_reason` never flags image_label, so the question can be drawn, served, billed and marked 0. Mitigating: all 12 live image_label questions in `etp_local` carry non-empty `detections_json`, so no current row has the shape - it is a latent authoring trap.

##### pm-ux-admin-2 - Release Results reveals every mark on one unconfirmed click
**high** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `views/assessment_views.xml:106-108`; `models/assessment.py:2656-2687`
- **What:** The assessment header's "Release Results" button has no `confirm=` and no count. It releases every submitted, unreleased attempt at once - including candidates whose subjective answers are still ungraded - and only warns about those *after* the write, in a toast. Release is irreversible: no un-release path exists anywhere in the module.
- **Evidence:** Every other destructive header button on the same form (Kill Scoring, Retry Failed Scoring, Cancel, Reset to Draft, Erase Candidate Data) carries a confirm; this one does not. Flutter requires a sheet first, with a Submitted / Releasing-now / Still-grading strip, a named list of still-grading candidates, a "This cannot be undone" notice, a "Wait for Scoring" escape and a counted "Release N result(s)" button.
- **Impact:** One stray click on the busiest screen in the product permanently shows a whole cohort marks that may still be pending, with nothing asked and nothing counted beforehand.
- **Fix:** Add a confirm naming the number being released and the number still grading, and put the count on the button label as Flutter does.
- **Verifier:** confirmed. Worth noting it is identical in the pre-build baseline, so this is a pre-existing gap the parity wave did not close, not a regression.

##### pm-ux-candidate-2 - A question the clock took away is shown to the candidate as "Incorrect", in red, beside the correct answer
**high** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `controllers/api/serializers.py:1106-1123` (mcq/msq branch of `released_answer_review_row`)
- **What:** The branch tests only `not response` / score >= max / partial / else Incorrect. An expiry placeholder *is* a response (created by `_auto_submit_expired` with `state='submitted'`, score 0), so it falls to the final else and is labelled "Incorrect" with kind `fail`. The subjective branch 20 lines below does check `response.auto_submitted` and answers "No Grade"; the objective branch was never given the same check.
- **Evidence:** Read directly, plus a probe confirming the client renders verdict "Incorrect" with `Tone.bad` and `hasInput` true for such a row. `_dimension_marks` computes `max_score` from the question's keyed dimensions regardless, so the placeholder scores 0 out of N > 0.
- **Impact:** Questions the candidate never saw are presented as wrong answers with "Correct Answer: …" printed underneath. On a paper where time ran out at question 12 of 20, eight questions are recorded against them as errors.
- **Fix:** Add `elif response.auto_submitted: verdict, kind = "Not answered", "info"` ahead of the score comparisons, mirroring the subjective branch.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### pm-ux-candidate-4 - The same Strengths-and-Weaknesses card shows two different pass marks for one sitting
**high** · confirmed · **reproduced** (probe) · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `lib/assessment/screens/member/my_performance_screen.dart:552` vs `:628` in the same file, and `screens/exam/exam_screen.dart:3366`
- **What:** `my_performance_screen.dart:552` builds the CategoryCard with `final double threshold = asm?.passThreshold ?? 70;`. A candidate never loads an Assessment record (`/api/v1/assessments` is a manager route), so `asm` is null and the card always uses 70. The answer-sheet copy of the same card uses the figure `_compute_result` actually applied, and the ThresholdBar 76 lines below in the *same file* already uses `r.ev.passMarkPercent(r.asm)`.
- **Evidence:** Probe confirms `serverPassThreshold` parses to 60.0 from a real candidate payload (`result.pass_threshold` is sent on every released candidate attempt). The card both prints the threshold ("against the 70% pass mark") and splits strengths from weaknesses on it.
- **Impact:** On a 60% paper, My Performance tells the candidate the bar is 70% and files categories scoring 60-69% under "Weakest areas", while See-my-answers calls those same categories strengths. The widget's own header comment says it exists so four surfaces "agree to the decimal".
- **Fix:** Replace line 552 with `final double threshold = s.ev.passMarkPercent(asm);` - the expression the bar in the same file already uses.
- **Verifier:** confirmed, including that the file's own comment admits the fallback.

##### pm-ux-admin-1 - Picking one question template silently inflates the run in Odoo and is refused in Flutter
**high** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/prompt.py:590-597, 642-654`; `static/src/fields/template_quotas/template_quotas.js:107-124`; `lib/assessment/state/app_store.dart:6781-6818`
- **What:** The template-quota widget pins "Questions to generate" to the sum of the chips, as the plan requires - and then `_onchange_min_questions_for_types` raises that number to the count of allowed question types, ignoring `shape_quota_json` entirely. On a generator that allows 4 types, a chip reading "x 1" leaves the field reading 4 with no message. Through the API the same act is refused by `_check_question_count` with an error naming question *types*, a control the operator never touched - and `setShapeQuotas` applies the chip optimistically with no rollback and no re-read, so the Flutter chip and count stay on screen as if saved.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced live: generator 323 (4 allowed types), count 10, pick one template -> chip "x 1", field reads 4. `POST /api/v1/generators/323/update {"shape_quotas":{"template:5341":1},"sop_question_count":1}` -> 422 "Questions to Generate (1) is less than the 4 selected question types…". The ORM write raises the same ValidationError. The rollback hook exists in `app_store` and is unused here.
- **Impact:** An Odoo admin who asks for one item of one shape pays for four; a Flutter admin sees a chip and a count the server rejected, and only finds out on the next reload.
- **Fix:** Count template quotas toward the type floor (or skip the floor when `shape_quota_json` is set), and give `setShapeQuotas` a rollback plus a re-read on failure.
- **Verifier:** confirmed on both surfaces.

##### pm-ux-candidate-1 - The answer sheet prints the system's auto-submit placeholder as the candidate's own answer
**high** · confirmed · **reproduced** (probe) · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `controllers/api/serializers.py:891-897, 1165`; written at `models/assessment.py:4372, 4429-4433`; rendered at `lib/assessment/screens/exam/exam_screen.dart:3427-3437`
- **What:** When an attempt settles, `_auto_submit_expired` creates a Response for every unanswered question with `justification = "[Auto-submitted: time expired]"` (or "[Submitted with unanswered questions]", or the proctoring variant). The serializer passes that string through untouched as `justification`, `AnswerSheetRow.hasInput` is true because it is non-empty, and `_AnswerCard` takes the else branch: `Eyebrow('Your answer')` followed by the placeholder, instead of "You did not answer this question."
- **Evidence:** Probe: `AnswerSheetRow.fromJson({'justification':'[Auto-submitted: time expired]'}, released: true)` gives `hasInput == true` and the placeholder as the text.
- **Impact:** Every timed-out, force-submitted or proctoring-ended sitting shows the candidate a page of their own questions with a bracketed internal system string quoted back as their answer, on the one screen that explains their marks.
- **Fix:** Blank `justification` in `released_answer_review_row` when `response.auto_submitted`, so the client's existing "You did not answer this question." branch fires.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### pm-ux-candidate-3 - "Your time has expired … your last answer was saved" is built by the server and thrown away by the client
**high** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Partly fixed - blocker B5** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `controllers/api/candidate.py:344-370` vs `lib/assessment/state/app_store.dart:5473`
- **What:** The backend deliberately saves the answer in flight before enforcing the deadline, then answers 409 `time_expired` with a message stating which of two things happened - "…and your last answer was saved." or "…but your last answer was incomplete and was not saved." - plus an `answer_saved` flag. `examAdvance`'s catch does `if (e.code == 'attempt_locked' || e.status == 409) { _markExamComplete(token); return true; }`, so every 409 is swallowed with no toast; grep for `answer_saved`/`answerSaved` across `lib/` returns nothing.
- **Evidence:** The route's own comment says it composes both branches "so the client can tell the candidate the truth either way"; the catch block's comment says "Show it once", which the code does not do. The next line toasts `e.message` for every other error.
- **Impact:** The single question a candidate has at the buzzer - was the answer I was typing kept? - goes unanswered, and a candidate whose payload was incomplete is never told their work was dropped.
- **Fix:** In `examAdvance`, before `_markExamComplete`, add `if (e.code == 'time_expired') toaster.show(e.message, ...)` - bad tone when `answer_saved` is false.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### swe-api-models-1 - W1 language guard does not cover the gateway's `auth='none'` sign-in routes
**medium** · unverified · not reproduced · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/ir_http.py:656-702`; `api_auth_gateway/controllers/main.py:175, 238, 280`
- **What:** The uninstalled-language swap runs only inside `_adopt_gateway_token`, called only from `_auth_method_user` / `_auth_method_public`. `/api/v1/auth_token`, `refresh_token`, `forgot_password` and `reset_password` are `auth='none'`, so a fresh no-cookie request keeps `lang = Accept-Language` (en_GB). Sign-in then reaches `_get_group_definitions`, which orders by a translated field, and `env.lang` raises `Invalid language code: en_GB` on a cold groups cache.
- **Evidence:** Odoo core `http.py:1780` (new session lang), `res_users.py:799-801` (has_group during authenticate), `res_groups.py:360-372` (translated order). The W1 HttpCase covers only `GET /api/v1/auth/me`; nothing tests `POST /auth_token`.
- **Impact:** After each deploy or pod restart, an en-GB browser that signs in before anything warms that pod's group cache is told its password is wrong - which pushes users to Forgot Password, the exact reset-email storm this work was meant to stop.
- **Fix:** Apply `_installed_lang` in an `IrHttp._auth_method_none` override (or in `_authenticate`) for API paths; add an HttpCase that clears the groups cache then POSTs `/api/v1/auth_token` with `Accept-Language: en-GB`.
- **Verifier:** no second pass ran on this one; the chain is from code reading only, on a read-only task with no database.

##### swe-logging-observability-1 - Reaching the $400/day or $20/candidate cap never logs a WARNING, and the same INFO line repeats every minute
**medium** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1914-1950, 1701-1712`; `services/vertex.py:1398-1428, 481-491`
- **What:** Five different events share one INFO line ("Scoring deferred for evaluator %s ... left pending"): daily cap, per-candidate cap, a Vertex 429 or the local rpm ceiling, a full DB pool, and a bearer-refresh serialization failure. A kill uses the same line and says "left pending" although the candidate lands in `cancelled`. Nothing logs at WARNING or above. When the daily cap bites, every 1-minute tick of every shard still re-plans up to 20 candidates.
- **Evidence:** `scoring.py:1944` is a single `_logger.info` for `VertexBudgetError`/`VertexCancelledError`/`VertexQuotaError`; `_check_spend` logs nothing; `_cron_llm_auto_score` has no early exit on a cap. The API layer logs the same pool-full condition at WARNING (`common.py:255`).
- **Impact:** The money cap stopping all grading, pool exhaustion caused by grading, and a return of the serialization storm cannot be alerted on. Meanwhile Loki fills with roughly 19k INFO lines an hour of identical deferrals.
- **Fix:** Log cap refusals and pool-full at WARNING with a stable tag (`SPEND_CAP daily`, `GRADING_POOL_FULL`), once per lane tick; end the tick on the first daily-cap refusal; log kills as "stopped", not "deferred".
- **Verifier:** confirmed line by line, including that the kill path logs "left pending" before `finish_evaluator` parks the row `cancelled`.

##### swe-logging-observability-2, swe-grading-1, swe-logging-observability-4, qa-backend-api-16 - Grading failures cannot be tied to a candidate, and per-answer failures are never logged at all
**medium** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1950-1955, 1396-1425, 2077`; `services/vertex.py:747, 966-1121`; `services/grading_cache.py` (all lines)
- **What:** The one ERROR line is literally `_logger.error("Scoring submission call failed", exc_info=error)` - no evaluator, no response ids, no model, no individual/bulk/cached flag. `_store_error` writes to the database and logs nothing on any branch: a missing result, a null score, a truncated labelling reply, an answer that exhausts its attempts and goes terminal, and a failed re-grade that keeps the old mark are all silent. This build also raised `scoring_parallel_calls` from 1 to 4, so several candidates' calls now interleave on `etp-grade` threads, and Odoo's log format carries no thread name.
- **Evidence:** `constants.py:140` is `(1, 8, 4)` against the baseline's `(1, 8, 1)`. `usage_ctx` already holds `evaluator_id`, but `_log_usage` prints only `note='submission(N)'`. The evaluator id appears only on the adjacent `done: scored=0/N` INFO line.
- **Impact:** The planned 24 h post-deploy log watch cannot tie a failure, a truncation or a fallback to a candidate or a call, and the one event that needs a human - an answer stuck in `error` with a 0 - cannot be alerted on or found from logs.
- **Fix:** Set a contextvar or LoggerAdapter in `_grade_on_own_cursor` / `_store_submission` carrying `ev`, `asmt` and `note`; log one WARNING per call listing failed resp ids with a reason code, and a separate WARNING when an answer reaches terminal `error`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed. Both halves hold; the failed re-grade is not entirely traceless (it writes `llm_error` and `llm_feedback`), so only log-side correlation is missing - which is why `swe-grading-1` alone was lowered to low before being merged here.

##### swe-logging-observability-3 - At batch 20 the cut-off retry and its WARNING are dead code, so "cut-off replies near 0" cannot be measured
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/vertex.py:1024-1054`; `services/scoring.py:1002-1042, 1969-1975`
- **What:** At the chosen batch size of 20 the first attempt asks for `min(64000, max(16000, 4000+2500*20))` = 54,000 output tokens, while the retry ceiling is `clamp(_RETRY_OUTPUT_TOKENS=32000)` = 32,000. The guard `attempt_tokens < retry_ceiling` is false, so neither the MAX_TOKENS retry nor the unparseable-JSON retry nor their WARNINGs ever fire. `_parse_results` then salvages whatever complete items it can, silently, and each missing item goes to `_store_error`, also silently.
- **Evidence:** Probe run against the real module code: `batch=8 first=24000 retry_ceiling=32000 -> retry+warning happens: True`; `batch=20 first=54000 -> False`; salvage produced no log output at all. `final_implementation_plan.md` §6 asks operators to watch "cut-off replies near 0".
- **Impact:** The rollout check the plan depends on has no WARNING signal and no ids. A large batch is also never re-asked with more room.
- **Fix:** Log a WARNING with the evaluator id, expected vs recovered item counts and the finish reason whenever the final reply is MAX_TOKENS or salvage was used; decide separately whether the retry ceiling should ever be below the first attempt.
- **Verifier:** confirmed, arithmetic re-run. One overstatement: truncation is still countable from the INFO line `Vertex result ... finish=MAX_TOKENS` - it just has no WARNING and no ids.

##### swe-logging-observability-6, swe-scale-cost-7 - Cache create/refresh spend and cache hits are missing from the "LLM usage" log stream
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** (measured on a stress run) · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/grading_cache.py:212-225, 173`; `services/vertex.py:742-753`
- **What:** `_book` writes cache create and refresh ledger rows straight through `_write_ledger_row`, never through `_log_usage`, so no `LLM usage: op=scoring_cache_create ... cost=$` line is ever written. The per-call usage line also prints `in=promptTokenCount` (which already includes cached tokens) with no `cached` field, no evaluator and no indication whether `cachedContent` was sent.
- **Evidence:** Stress ledger: average `tokens_in` 5,120 of which `cached_tokens` 4,135; the one `scoring_cache_create` row ($0.0131) had no matching log line. The team's prod cost figures come from Grafana/Loki, not the database.
- **Impact:** Once the cache switch is on, spend totalled from logs either prices 4,135 cached tokens at full rate or cannot see cache hits at all, and misses storage cost entirely. Billing itself is correct - only log-derived analysis is wrong.
- **Fix:** Emit the same INFO line from `_book`, and add `cached=%d ev=%s cache=%s` to the usage line.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; caps are unaffected because `_spend_since` reads the database ledger, which does hold these rows.

##### swe-grading-2, swe-logging-observability-7 - Candidate answer text and PII reach the server logs
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** (probe) · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:961-969, 1225-1227, 1950`; `services/vertex.py:828, 1121-1124`; `models/assessment.py:1970, 2018, 2034, 2175, 4258-4261, 4284-4287`
- **What:** (a) The positive-deduction WARNING logs the judge's free-text `reason`, and `prompts/scoring.md:42` explicitly tells the judge to quote the worker ("missed 'navy velvet sofa' (wrote 'a blue couch')"). (b) `_parse_results` raises `ValueError("Could not parse JSON from scoring response: %s" % text[:200])` and `LLMRefusalError` carries `t[:200]`; both are logged at ERROR with a traceback. (c) VIOLATION and provisioning lines log `partner_name`, email and the assessment name during live sittings.
- **Evidence:** Probe printed `judge emitted a POSITIVE deduction (25.0) for "wrote 'my name is Priya Sharma, priya@example.com'"`. `services/audit.py:26-30` states names and emails must stay out of Loki.
- **Impact:** Worker answers and candidate PII land in a log store several teams can read, against the product rule and the project's own audit policy. Mostly pre-existing, not introduced by this build.
- **Fix:** Log ids and lengths, never text: resp id plus the deduction's point value, reply length plus finish reason, applicant/evaluator ids in VIOLATION and provisioning lines. Keep the excerpt in the admin-only `llm_reasoning`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed on every limb.

##### swe-scale-cost-1 - A 704-candidate paper models at about 54-62 min, not the planned 35-45 min
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** (stress harness + simulation) · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:2819, 2865-2867`; cron cadence in Odoo core; app poll cap `assessment_detail_screen.dart:156`
- **What:** Three things add up. (a) At `db_maxconn` 64 with 4 shards each lane gets `room = (32-8)//8 = 3` calls, not the 4 the setting shows, so 12 are in flight not 16. (b) `_drain_in_parallel` always finishes the oldest candidate first (`in_flight.popleft()` then `pending.result()`), so one slow call idles the other slots. (c) Every tick runs to zero and the next tick waits for the minute grid because nothing calls `_trigger()`.
- **Evidence:** Shell on the 750-candidate fixture printed "parallel calls/lane 3". Stress harness (fake Vertex, 1.0 s ±40%, 4 lanes x 3 slots): 795 calls in 90 s against 66 s ideal, 73% slot use. Simulation at 45 s calls: 3 calls/lane = 54-62 min; 4 calls/lane = 43-51 min. `scoring_speed_plan.md:106` itself claims 64 "allows 4 calls per lane".
- **Impact:** The plan's ~35-45 min becomes about an hour, and the app's detail watch stops after 720 ticks x 5 s = 60 min (see `swe-scale-cost-4`), so the screen can stop updating before grading ends.
- **Fix:** Store whichever candidate finishes first (`FIRST_COMPLETED`); re-trigger the lane's cron when a tick hits its limit; set `db_maxconn` to 80+ to actually get 4 calls per lane.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; arithmetic re-run for pools 64/80/96 - 80 gives exactly 4. A real plan-vs-build divergence, not just a tuning miss.

##### swe-grading-8, qa-backend-api-2 - A Retry/Queue/Re-score click cancels a Kill that is still stopping a run
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:5044-5046, 4939-4941, 4903-4904, 2411, 2640-2643`
- **What:** After a Kill, `scoring_cancel_requested` stays raised on purpose so the lane's remaining dispatched calls are refused. `action_rescore_individually`, `action_reset_failed_scoring`, `action_queue_llm_score` and `action_llm_score_all` all call `_withdraw_scoring_kill()` unconditionally - before the busy check and before they queue anything. A click that resets 0 answers, or targets a different candidate on the same paper, still lowers the flag.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: batch size 2, fake Vertex sleeping 8 s. During call 1, kill returned 200 and the flag read `t`; `POST /scoring/requeue_errored` for a *different* candidate returned `answers_reset=0`, after which the flag read `f`. Call 2 was then sent and the candidate finished `scored` instead of `cancelled`. A control run with no click refused call 2 correctly.
- **Impact:** Kill does not reliably stop spending. Flutter's "Re-score This Assessment" calls `requeueFailed` first, so one click on the same paper undoes a Kill that is still in flight.
- **Fix:** Withdraw the kill only when the action actually queued or reset something, and never while `_being_graded()` holds candidates of that paper.
- **Verifier:** confirmed at every call site.

##### swe-api-models-3, qa-backend-api-4 - Empty or malformed `question_ids` silently widens a chosen re-score to every unresolved answer
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `controllers/api/common.py:448-463`; `controllers/api/admin.py:1693-1695`
- **What:** `id_list_arg` drops non-integers and returns `[]` for `[]`, `'abc'`, `[{...}]` or `{...}`. The route then does `id_list_arg("question_ids") or None`, and `None` means "no ids", which the model reads as "every needs_llm answer that is not scored". Plan W6 says only an *absent* key means today's set.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: `POST /attempts/129972/rescore {question_ids:'abc'}` returned 200 with `queued=4` and four keys written; `[{'x':1}]` and `{'a':1}` did the same. A valid id not on the attempt correctly got 422 `not_on_attempt`.
- **Impact:** A client bug or an old build sending the wrong shape turns "Re-score this answer" into a whole-candidate re-score: extra paid calls and extra audit lines. It stays within one candidate, so the individual-stays-individual rule holds.
- **Fix:** Tell "key absent" from "key present but unusable" and answer 422 `invalid` for the second.
- **Verifier:** confirmed by running `id_list_arg` directly on each shape.

##### swe-odoo-ui-1 - The status badge never starts auto-refreshing after the admin presses a queue button
**medium** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `static/src/fields/auto_refresh/auto_refresh.js:62-75, 120-125`; `models/prompt.py:691-701`; `models/assessment.py:2416-2426` (also Extract Tags, Retry Failed Scoring, Score Subjective, Re-score This Answer)
- **What:** Every queue button returns a `display_notification` with no `next`, so the form is never reloaded and the badge keeps its old value ("Idle"/"Done", or stays hidden) until the admin refreshes by hand. The widget also only schedules a poll from `onWillStart` and `_poll` - there is no `onWillUpdateProps` - so a `model.load()` that hands an always-mounted badge a now-busy record never starts polling.
- **Evidence:** Odoo 19 `client_actions.js:23` returns `params.next` (undefined), `form_controller.js:643` `afterExecuteActionButton` is empty, and `record.js:1105-1113` skips the reload when the record is clean. `form_controller.xml:46` renders the Renderer with no `t-key`, so a reload reuses the same component instances. The notification text itself says "refresh to see them".
- **Impact:** Auto-refresh does not work on its main path: press Generate or Run Evaluation, then watch, and nothing happens.
- **Fix:** Add `"next": {"type": "ir.actions.act_window_close"}` to those notifications, and give the widget an `onWillUpdateProps` that resets `_delay`/`_lastSeen` and calls `_maybeSchedule`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; the whole chain was traced. Pre-existing in part, but the widget was reworked in this build.

##### swe-odoo-ui-2, swe-scale-cost-5, pm-ux-admin-10 - The Candidates tab polls for ever, with a spinner, for candidates nobody queued
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** (measured in a headless browser) · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `views/assessment_views.xml:433-436`; `static/src/fields/auto_refresh/auto_refresh.js:45-48`
- **What:** `pending` is in the widget's busy set, but it is also the default `llm_state` of every evaluator - invited, in progress, or submitted with auto-grade off. Every visible row shows "Pending" with a spinner and "auto-refreshing…", and reads its own record for ever. Every root reload rebuilds the x2many rows, so each busy row remounts and its backoff restarts at 3 s.
- **Evidence:** Playwright on a 750-candidate paper, 10 rows at `pending` with `scoring_requested=False` and nothing being graded: 132 reads in 240 s (steady state ~24 requests/min per open form). A second run on a cancelled paper: 30 `evaluator/read` calls in 60 s over 5 such rows. The repo's own comment at `assessment_views.xml:21` rejects this widget for a list because it is "one timer per row".
- **Impact:** The roster claims grading is in flight for people who have not sat the exam - the very signal an admin scans that column for - and a forgotten tab makes ~11,500 reads per 8 hours. The backoff added in this build does not hold on this list.
- **Fix:** Give the widget a per-use busy set (or treat `pending` as busy only when `scoring_requested` is set), and batch the row reads into one call per list.
- **Verifier:** confirmed end to end, including the remount that resets the backoff.

##### swe-odoo-ui-3 - The badge's settle reload throws away the admin's unsaved edits
**medium** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `static/src/fields/auto_refresh/auto_refresh.js:154-159`
- **What:** When the server value leaves the busy set, the widget calls `rec.model.root.load()` with no dirty check. `Record._load` -> `_setData` (no `keepChanges`) sets `this._changes = {}`, so anything typed and not yet saved is silently discarded. On the assessment form this fires whenever *any* visible candidate row settles.
- **Evidence:** Odoo 19 `record.js:254-258, 803-812, 106-111`. `prompt_views.xml` locks only the type and quota fields while a run is busy, so `name` and the free-text fields stay editable.
- **Impact:** Lost form input (not database data). Admins will hit it whenever generation or grading finishes while they are typing.
- **Fix:** If `rec.model.root.dirty`, skip the auto-reload and show a "changed on server, reload" hint instead.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### swe-odoo-ui-4 - Template chips set "Questions to generate" from counts they neither show nor clean up
**medium** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `static/src/fields/template_quotas/template_quotas.js:106-121`; `views/prompt_views.xml:269-293`
- **What:** `setCount` sums *every* key in `shape_quota_json` into `sop_question_count`, including built-in type counts (`"mcq": 2`) the widget never renders. Removing a type from the Odoo many2many leaves that type's quota behind: the API route prunes it, nothing in Odoo does.
- **Evidence:** `template_quotas.xml` renders only `template:*` and "Missing form" chips. No ORM prune exists - `prompt.write` touches file/name only, the sole onchange just raises the count, and the allow-list re-parse lives in `controllers/api/write.py` alone. `vertex.py:6268` then uses `max(pinned_count, quota_total)`.
- **Impact:** Flutter sets `mcq x2`, the admin removes MCQ in Odoo and adds "Compare two edits x1": the count is pinned at 3 and the run authors 2 unrequested generic items, paid for. Even with valid counts, the total does not match the visible chips.
- **Fix:** Prune type keys not in `allowed_question_type_ids` on write/onchange (the same `parse_shape_quotas` call the API uses), and show type counts read-only in the widget.
- **Verifier:** confirmed, including that the dropped `mcq:2` becomes 2 paid generic items.

##### swe-odoo-ui-9, pm-ux-admin-9 - Two candidate buttons do exactly the same thing, one is named for a reset that never happens, and neither is manager-only
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `views/assessment_views.xml:812-819`; `models/assessment.py:4977-5026`
- **What:** "Score Subjective" (visible on any submitted attempt) and "Reset & Re-score Errored" (visible when `llm_state == 'error'`) both call `action_rescore_individually()` with no arguments, so they are identical and neither resets anything. On a submitted attempt that errored, both sit side by side. Neither carries `groups=`, while the new "Re-score This Answer" does. "Score Subjective" also shows on a fully scored attempt, where its only outcome is a warning.
- **Evidence:** Live attempt 1510 renders both; live attempt 4354 (fully scored) answers "Nothing to re-score." `ir.model.access.csv:30` gives `group_assessment_manager_restricted` read-only on the evaluator, so a read-only manager sees a spend button that fails on write.
- **Impact:** Two identical controls with different promises on the screen used to unstick one candidate, plus a third that is usually a no-op - the pattern the assessment-level Kill button was explicitly fixed to stop doing.
- **Fix:** Keep one button, label it with the count of unresolved answers as Flutter does, hide it at zero, and add `groups="assessments_be_v2.group_assessment_manager"`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed on both the duplication and the missing groups.

##### swe-flutter-2, qa-flutter-ui-4 - The candidate page shows no queued state after "Re-score N answer(s)" and never refreshes
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** (widget test + live run) · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `lib/assessment/screens/admin/attempt_detail_screen.dart:80, 88, 302-313, 380-392`; `responses_screen.dart` rows
- **What:** The route used to grade inside the request, so the page showed new marks afterwards; it now only queues. The page loads the attempt in `initState`/`didUpdateWidget` only, renders `Pill.state(r.llmState)` with no `rescoreRequested` branch, keeps the same enabled button, and never re-reads when the grade lands. The closing `refresh(background:true)` runs `_loadAdmin`, whose 12-slot fan-out contains no attempts call.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced in a scratch copy: after tapping "Re-score 1 answer(s)" with `{queued:1}`, the button stayed enabled, 0 widgets contained "queued", and 0 requests were made over 3 simulated minutes. Live run: same, while the server *had* recorded the key (the answer page showed a disabled "Re-score queued").
- **Impact:** Operators see stale marks and errored states until they reload by hand, and will press again or conclude it did nothing. A repeat press is harmless server-side (`new = chosen.filtered(lambda r: not r.rescore_request_key)`), but the toast still says "Queued N".
- **Fix:** Show a per-answer "Re-score queued" chip and a disabled or relabelled button on the candidate page; reuse the answer page's light watch while any answer on the attempt is queued.
- **Verifier:** confirmed. Mitigating: `app_store.dart:4711` does set `rescoreRequested` optimistically and a toast fires, so the press is acknowledged even though the page state is not.

##### swe-flutter-3, qa-flutter-ui-2 - The active state or scoring chip disappears while its filter is still applied
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `lib/assessment/screens/admin/assessment_detail_screen.dart:2998-3042, 2764-2792`
- **What:** Chips are hidden at count 0 (`if (!haveCounts || (counts[wire] ?? 0) > 0)`) with no exemption for the pressed filter, and `_state` is reset only when the assessment id changes. Counts come from `meta.counts`, computed under search and flagged but *not* under the pressed state, and they move when a run ends and the tab refetches.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced twice. Widget test: press "Score Pending 2", set score_pending to 0, reload with that state - the chip is gone. Live: chips became "All 4 | Submitted 4 | Scored 4 | Flagged", none pressed, table "No candidate matches these filters."
- **Impact:** The filter is invisible and the operator sees an empty table with no explanation. The most natural trigger is the end of a re-score run watched from this tab - the workflow these chips were added for.
- **Fix:** Always render the chip equal to `_state`, even at count 0, or reset `_state` to '' (and refetch) when its count drops to 0.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; the run-ended branch re-fetches with the stale `_state` still set.

##### qa-backend-api-3 - The kill flag stays raised after the in-flight lane finishes, and later submissions are parked "cancelled by an admin"
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:2598, 2642-2643, 2861-2880`; `services/scoring.py:1619`
- **What:** `_settle_scoring_cancelled` lowers `scoring_cancel_requested` only `if not held`. If every held call returns successfully, nothing lowers it: the phase reads `idle` while the flag is still up, and the next candidate queued by auto-grade on submit is settled as cancelled by `_auto_score_eligible` without being graded.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: killed paper 24698 with 4 parallel calls in flight; they completed and were stored, and after the tick `scoring_cancel_requested=t` with `/scoring` reporting phase idle. A late candidate then sat and submitted: 0 Vertex calls, `llm_state=cancelled`, `llm_error` "Scoring cancelled by an admin - stopped before the grader reached this candidate."
- **Impact:** Candidates who submit after a finished, killed run go ungraded until an admin re-queues them, and are shown as stopped by an admin. It self-heals after burning one candidate.
- **Fix:** Lower the paper's flag at the end of a lane's tick (or in `finish_evaluator`) when no candidate of that paper is still held or queued.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### qa-backend-api-5, swe-api-models-12, apc-5, swe-odoo-ui-11, pm-ux-admin-11 - Two JSON import lanes still write straight into the live bank, and the button says "Import as drafts"
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `controllers/api/write.py:2308` (payload lane); `models/bank_import_wizard.py:408-433` (native lane); `views/bank_import_views.xml:52-55` (button label)
- **What:** W9 decides that imported questions, CSV and JSON, land as drafts in Pending Approvals. The CSV lane was fixed and the authoring-harness JSON lane already produced drafts, but two lanes did not change: the wizard's native round-trip JSON calls `import_bank_native` and writes live bank questions, and `POST /bank/import` with `payload={project, question_bank}` creates an active `assessments.be.question` directly. The wizard's single footer button is labelled "Import as drafts" for every format, and the format is detected from the file, so the operator cannot choose.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: the payload import returned `questions_created=1` and the database holds question 42583 "Question 1", active, with no draft row; CSV and harness files created drafts 7605-7609. Through the wizard, a native payload reported "Rebuilt 1 question(s) from the round-trip export", bank +1, drafts +0. A `question_bank`-shaped JSON sent as a *file* gets the CSV error "CSV must have at least a title or prompt column".
- **Impact:** A file dropped on a button that promises review can land unreviewed questions in the live bank - the one outcome the "drafts first" decision exists to prevent. The route is `@require_manager`, and no Flutter caller uses the payload lane today.
- **Fix:** Owner decision. If "drafts", route both lanes through the drafts path like CSV; if the round-trip restore is exempt, amend `admin_console_plan.md` §3, relabel the button per detected format, and give an unknown-shape JSON file a JSON-specific error.
- **Verifier:** confirmed on both lanes. Already tracked: `CHANGE_SUMMARY_for_review.md:25` lists the native lane as an open owner decision - but not the payload lane.

##### qa-grading-edge-2 - The image_label reply check looks at the wrong field: a missing `box_scores` is a silent 0, a missing `score` is an error
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:2003-2011, 2045-2062`
- **What:** The labelling mark comes only from `box_scores`, but the "no usable score" guard tests the top-level `score`, and the retry needs `returned > 0`. So on a first grade a reply with `score`/`deductions` but no `box_scores` (or `{}`, or a list) is stored as scored 0 with no retry and no `needs_review` flag; while a reply with complete `box_scores` and no `score` is rejected as "Grader returned no score", costs 3 paid calls, and ends in `error` with 0. A re-grade handles both safely because the old mark is kept.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: "empty-box_scores", "missing-box_scores-key" and "box-scores-as-list" all gave judge score 70 stored as 0, flags None, calls=1. `box_scores {1:95,2:95,3:95}` with no score gave calls=3 then `error`, raw 0.
- **Impact:** A labelling answer can be permanently failed at 0 with nothing flagged, including on the gemini-2.5-pro fallback and the cached path whose items carry no question_type.
- **Fix:** For image_label, treat "attempted boxes with no box score" as retryable even at `returned == 0`, and decide "usable result" from `box_scores` rather than the top-level score.
- **Verifier:** confirmed, and the in-code justification ("an empty box_scores is also what an unparsed or refused reply looks like") does not hold - an unparsed reply raises earlier and a refused one is errored one block earlier.

##### qa-grading-edge-3 - A cache Vertex rejects on use is re-created for every candidate, with no circuit breaker
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:1875-1879`; `services/grading_cache.py:111, 122, 159, 200-209`
- **What:** When a cached call returns 404, or 400/403 mentioning "cache", the row is expired and the call goes inline. `forget()` writes only `expires_at`, never `failed_until`, so the next candidate finds no live cache, `create=True` and no backoff - and pays for a fresh create that will be rejected the same way. `failed_until` guards failed *creates* only.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: 6 candidates on a shared 3-question paper with every cached `generateContent` returning 403 "Permission denied on resource cachedContents/..": creates=6, cached attempts=6, inline=6, 6 `scoring_cache_create` ledger rows ($0.094 at 5k tokens). All candidates scored, so the waste is silent.
- **Impact:** If caching is on and cache use fails persistently (IAM, location mismatch, API change), every bulk candidate pays an extra create plus a wasted round trip - roughly $15 per 704-candidate paper at ~7k-token groups, with latency doubled. Cost only, and only with the switch on.
- **Fix:** When a cached call misses shortly after its own create (or after N misses per key), set `failed_until` so the group stays inline for 10 minutes.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; no counter or breaker exists anywhere in the module.

##### pm-ux-admin-5 - Odoo's LLM Budget shows no today figure and no daily cap
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/llm_dashboard.py:17-44`; `views/llm_dashboard_views.xml`
- **What:** The dashboard is an all-time snapshot - total cost, tokens, thinking tokens, requests, images, videos, average per request - with no period filter and no reference to the $400/day or $20/candidate caps. Flutter leads its budget screen with a Today panel: spend, cap, percent of cap, remaining, and a "daily cap reached" notice.
- **Evidence:** Rendered live: "Live snapshot · refreshed on open", "$82.9155 TOTAL COST", "184 REQUESTS", no date control anywhere; the model defines no daily or cap field.
- **Impact:** An Odoo-only admin cannot answer "can we grade this cohort today?", and when the cap bites and grading stops this screen looks perfectly healthy.
- **Fix:** Add today's spend against the configured daily and per-candidate caps to the dashboard header, reusing the figures `/api/v1/budget` already computes.
- **Verifier:** confirmed but lowered from high: today's spend *is* reachable in Odoo through the LLM Usage list's Day group-by, so the gap is cap awareness on the dashboard, not a total absence.

##### pm-ux-admin-7 - Odoo's Form Studio button keeps the name Flutter deliberately abandoned as misleading
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `views/studio_form_views.xml:58-66`; `lib/assessment/screens/admin/form_designer_screen.dart:111-122`
- **What:** The primary action reads "Send to Candidates". It sends nothing to candidates: it mints bank questions, a generator and a *draft* assessment, and a separate Launch & Invite is what reaches people. Flutter renamed the identical action to "Publish" / "Confirm Publish" for exactly this reason. Odoo's confirm also omits the two facts Flutter's sheet leads with - that nothing reaches candidates until launch, and how many questions the form becomes.
- **Evidence:** Live forms 1865 and 6461 render the button; Flutter's comment says the old name "contradicted its own tooltip … an examiner who read the button literally had every reason to think a half-finished form had just gone out to a cohort".
- **Impact:** The same decision reads two ways: the console says a draft was created, Odoo says a cohort was mailed.
- **Fix:** Rename to "Publish" and reuse Flutter's confirm wording, including the question count and "Nothing reaches candidates until you launch it."
- **Verifier:** confirmed but lowered from high, because the confirm text an admin must pass does describe the real outcome.

##### pm-ux-admin-8 - Opening "New Template" and leaving the page saves an empty "Untitled task" into the shared picker
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Partly fixed (B4-21)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/prompt.py:501-508`; `views/prompt_views.xml:396-402`
- **What:** "New Template" opens a task-template form pre-filled from context defaults, which leaves the record dirty on arrival. Navigating away fires Odoo's `beforeUnload` urgent save - which has no dirty check and never short-circuits for a new record - so a blank, active template named "Untitled task" is written. The quota picker lists every active template with no generator filter, so the junk appears in every generator's dropdown.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced twice on a live instance: template count 4 -> 5 without touching a field or pressing Save; rows 5344 and 5345 both "Untitled task", `origin_prompt_id 323`, `active = t`. Mechanism verified in Odoo core (`form_controller.js:501-506`, `record.js:1105`).
- **Impact:** The template library and every generator's picker accumulate empty entries that generate nothing, and an admin picking by name can choose one.
- **Fix:** Open the new template through a dialog the admin must explicitly save (as the console does), or refuse to save a template with no name and no items.
- **Verifier:** confirmed, mechanism traced into core.

##### pm-ux-admin-12 - "Question Drafts" lists approved questions, keeps telling the admin to review them, and its buttons silently do nothing
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `views/prompt_views.xml:202-211, 496-520`; `models/prompt.py:2572-2574, 3288-3292`
- **What:** The green banner is gated on `sop_gen_state == 'done' and question_count != 0`, never on the draft count, so it stays for ever once a generator has produced anything - still saying "Review them under Question Drafts below … Approve the ones you want". The tab binds the unfiltered `question_ids`, so it lists approved and denied rows too under the heading "Drafts", with "Approve Selected" and "Deny Selected" in its header. Both actions filter to `state == 'draft'` and `return True`, changing nothing and reporting nothing.
- **Evidence:** Live generator 323: 10 questions, all approved, Pending Approvals empty, banner present, tab lists all 10 with STATE "Approved". `rows.action_deny()` returned True with the tally unchanged; `action_approve()` likewise.
- **Impact:** A finished generator permanently advertises work that does not exist, and the two bulk buttons offered there are no-ops with no feedback either way.
- **Fix:** Gate the banner on the count of rows still in `draft`, scope the tab to pending drafts (or rename it and add a state filter), and have both actions report how many rows they skipped.
- **Verifier:** confirmed on all three limbs.

##### pm-ux-admin-4 - Kill Scoring reports a stale cumulative count to the Flutter console
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `controllers/api/admin.py:561-567`
- **What:** The kill route ignores what `action_kill_scoring` actually settled and recounts `settled` as every evaluator on the assessment whose `llm_state == 'cancelled'` - including rows parked by earlier kills. A kill that stopped nothing therefore answers a positive `settled_count`, which Flutter renders as "Stopped grading - N candidate(s) settled".
- **Evidence:** Reproduced: kill #1 with one candidate queued returned `settled_count = 1` (correct). Kill #2 with nothing queued returned `settled_count = 1` again, while Odoo's own notification correctly read "Nothing to stop / No candidate was being graded on this assessment".
- **Impact:** The two consoles give contradictory answers to the same act, and the wrong one is the console most admins use. On a paper with kill history it reports the lifetime total of cancelled candidates.
- **Fix:** Return the `(settled, cleared)` tuple `_settle_scoring_cancelled` already computes, and let the toast say "nothing to stop" at zero.
- **Verifier:** confirmed but lowered from high: the message is wrong, no behaviour or money is. Byte-identical in the baseline, so pre-existing.

##### pm-ux-candidate-6 - A red "This answer is incomplete for its question type" fires mid-answer on an answer the server has safely stored
**medium** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `lib/assessment/state/app_store.dart:5175-5184, 5666-5677`; `controllers/api/candidate.py:372-377, 988-993, 1046-1049`
- **What:** The debounced autosave fires 5 s after any keystroke or pick once `Response.hasInput` is true (one option is enough). For an image_ab question with "require justification" on, `_record_response` holds the answer as a *draft* and returns False, which the route turns into 422 `incomplete_answer`, and the client calls `toaster.bad` with the server's sentence. `_answerSent` is written only on acceptance, so the toast repeats on the next change.
- **Evidence:** Read of the gate, the draft write and the toast path.
- **Impact:** A candidate who answers an A/B question the natural way - verdicts first, write-up second - gets a destructive-red error in server vocabulary over an answer that is safely stored. During a timed exam that reads as data loss.
- **Fix:** On the "stay" autosave, treat `incomplete_answer` as a draft hold: no toast, or an inert "Saved - this question still needs a justification". `examAdvance` already surfaces the real refusal when it matters.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### pm-ux-admin-3 - A queued individual re-score is invisible in Odoo on both screens where it is requested
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)

Nothing persists that on screen: no field, badge or invisible condition anywhere in the views reads `rescore_request_key`, so the answer form, the attempt form and the roster show no queued state and the button stays enabled with the same label. Flutter relabels the same control "Re-score queued" and disables it.

The assessment header does show it ("1 queued · 2 scored"), so the data reaches one surface and not the two the admin was just on.

##### pm-ux-admin-13 - Odoo offers paid re-grading on a cancelled assessment; Flutter refuses to show the button there
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Partly fixed (B4-02, B2-11)** (§7.2)

Flutter excludes cancelled explicitly, with the reason in its source: the button spends an LLM call per answer, so offering it on a paper somebody called off is offering paid re-grading of abandoned work.

##### pm-ux-admin-15 - Killing a run drops queued individual re-scores, and only Odoo ever says so
**medium** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:2553-2574, 2646-2654`; `controllers/api/admin.py:565-567`; `views/assessment_views.xml:76-79`
- **What:** `action_kill_scoring` clears every queued `rescore_request_key` on the assessment and reports the count in its Odoo notification. The API route returns only `settled_count`, so the Flutter console cannot mention the dropped re-scores at all - on the surface where per-answer re-score is the headline control. Neither confirm dialog warns beforehand.
- **Evidence:** `_settle_scoring_cancelled` returns `(settling, cleared)` and the notification reports "%d re-score request(s) cancelled"; the route's `ok({…})` carries `assessment_id` and `settled_count` only, and the Flutter toast builder reads `settledCount`/`settled`/`cancelled` only.
- **Impact:** An admin who queued individual re-scores and then stops a cohort run loses those requests, and in the console is never told - so they wait for grades that will never arrive.

- **Verifier:** confirmed; every link verified in source although not reproduced at runtime.

##### pm-ux-candidate-8 - A candidate whose written answers are still being graded sees a bare grey "Pending" over real marks
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** (probe) · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `controllers/api/serializers.py:421, 488-547`; `lib/assessment/domain/models.dart:5226-5227`
- **What:** `candidate_result` puts the count at `result.subjective_pending`, but `Attempt.fromJson` parses `subjective['pending']` - the *admin* roster shape. A candidate payload has no `subjective` object at all, so `subjectivePending` is always 0 on every candidate surface. The completion screen and the My Assessments card then show a grey "Pending" pill and nothing else.
- **Evidence:** Probe: an attempt built from the real candidate shape with `subjective_pending: 4` parses to `ev.subjectivePending == 0`. Grepping `lib/` for "still grading" / "being graded" finds only admin screens and one answer-sheet sub-line.
- **Impact:** A candidate opens a released result, sees "3 / 10" and a grey "Pending", and reasonably concludes they failed - when four written answers are unmarked and the total can only rise.
- **Fix:** Add `result.subjective_pending` to the parse chain and say "N written answers are still being marked - your total may rise" on the completion screen and the attempt card.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### pm-ux-candidate-12 - Marker geometry is handed to the candidate for exactly the question types whose baked overlay the server refuses to serve
**medium** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Regressed - blocker B2** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `controllers/api/candidate.py:826-841` (`_label_boxes`) vs `controllers/media_stream.py:325-342` (`annotated_is_worker_safe`); rendered via `models.dart:839-863` and `answer_layouts.dart:1857-1861`
- **What:** `annotated_is_worker_safe` returns True only for `detection_mode` in (`ui`, `dense`, `dense_boxes`) or a live-DOM capture, because for anything else "the markers are drawn ON the defects, so the overlay IS the answer key" (its own docstring, Finding L-2). `_label_boxes` applies no such gate: whenever every entry in `detections_json` carries `box_2d` it returns `{number, box_2d}` pairs, and `StimulusPlate` draws an interactive numbered overlay client-side. `detection_mode` defaults to `object`, which is not in the safe set.
- **Evidence:** Read of both gates plus the default; `detections_json` with geometry is written for every lane including the object one. The `_label_boxes` docstring's justification ("the geometry only repeats what the annotated picture already shows") is false precisely in that case.
- **Impact:** For the default image_label question the candidate is shown, drawn by the client, exactly the marker positions the server declines to bake in. Either that is a hint leak on a graded question or the security gate is over-strict - the two channels cannot both be right, and today the candidate gets the more generous one.
- **Fix:** Gate the geometry branch of `_label_boxes` on the same predicate `media_stream` uses, falling back to bare numbers. Flag to whoever owns Finding L-2 for the final call.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### apc-3, swe-flutter-4 - The deploy note's mitigation for old admin-written verdicts is not built
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `controllers/api/serializers.py:1212`; rendered at `lib/assessment/screens/exam/exam_screen.dart:3455-3464`
- **What:** `final_implementation_plan.md:403-414` says: candidates now see the grader's verdict on released answers, verdicts written under the old instructions were meant for admins, and "if any contain internal terms, show candidates only verdicts written under the new instructions". The precheck that *finds* them exists; the fix that *hides* them does not. `score_verdict` is sent for any scored subjective answer with no reference to `llm_prompt_version` (that field appears in `controllers/` only in the admin audit payload).
- **Evidence:** The pre-W12 prompt stated "`feedback` IS THE ONLY THING YOU WRITE THAT THE CANDIDATE READS. Everything else … is internal and admin-only", so historical verdicts may name profiles, caps, thresholds or point arithmetic. The precheck printed "verdicts naming grading mechanics: 0 of 36" - but that 36 is local scratch data, not prod's ~1,000 graded answers.
- **Impact:** If the prod scan turns up such verdicts, the only options at push time are to ship the leak or stop the push - which conflicts with "one push".
- **Fix:** Add the one-line gate now: send `score_verdict` only when `llm_prompt_version` equals the new fingerprint (`bundled:3702673a`), behind a system parameter, so the scan's outcome is not a push blocker.
- **Verifier:** confirmed. Narrower than `swe-flutter-4` claimed on its own: the backend already sent `score_verdict` at HEAD and the same block already rendered credits and deductions whose `reason` text came from the same admin-only prompt, so this adds one line to an existing class of leak.

##### apc-4 - W6 reintroduces a "busy" refusal the plan explicitly removed, under a new code
**medium** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Resolved (owner decision 2026-09-23)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:5011-5017`; `controllers/api/admin.py:1694-1697`
- **What:** The decided behaviour (plan W6; `scoring_speed_plan.md` 5.1) is "drop the in-request grading and the 409 `scoring_busy`", and the cases table promises that clicking "Re-score 3 answer(s)" on a candidate whose lane is running simply queues them, with the overlap resolved by "whichever saves first wins (at most one call wasted)". The build instead raises `RescoreRefused(..., "being_graded")` whenever `question_ids` are supplied and `_being_graded()` is true, and the route answers 409.
- **Evidence:** `scoring_speed_plan.md:198` states "the 409 `scoring_busy` goes away" and `:214` gives the promised new behaviour; `admin.py:1680-1682` documents "409 `being_graded`, nothing queued". Flutter surfaces the server's words verbatim, so the admin sees the refusal.
- **Impact:** During a bulk run an admin who picks specific answers on an in-flight candidate gets the same class of rejection the plan set out to remove, just renamed.
- **Fix:** Either get the refusal decided and correct the two plan docs, or queue the request and let the "whichever saves first wins" rule handle the overlap as decided. The reasoning behind the refusal is sound - a key written over a row mid-grade collides with the lane's paid result - it simply was not the decision taken.
- **Verifier:** confirmed; the code choice is defensible, the docs still promise the opposite.

##### swe-grading-4, qa-backend-api-9, qa-grading-edge-10 - The new 32k grading retry goes beyond the approved plan and can cost 4 billed calls per attempt
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Decided (owner 2026-09-23)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `services/scoring.py:228-232, 1812-1814, 1834-1867`; `services/vertex.py:1024-1054`
- **What:** W12 asked only for a 16k output floor. The build also passes `retry_max_tokens=32000`, so any call of 11 answers or fewer (16.5k-31.5k) is now re-sent at double room on MAX_TOKENS *or* on unparseable JSON; before, only calls of 4 answers or fewer were. Nested inside `_grade_job`'s re-ask loop that is up to 4 billed calls per attempt, 12 across 3 attempts. More tokens do not fix a reply that was never cut off.
- **Evidence:** Reproduced with fake Vertex in "garbage" mode: one individual re-score made 4 calls at maxOutputTokens 16000, 32000, 16000, 32000. `test_a_grading_retry_doubles_past_the_floor` confirms the intent; `CHANGE_SUMMARY` line 17 documents "retry 32k" although plan W12 says only 16k.
- **Impact:** More paid calls than the design on cut-off or garbled replies; a candidate-crafted overflow costs about 2x more per job than before. Bounded by the existing caps.
- **Fix:** Owner decision - drop the override, or keep it but retry only on MAX_TOKENS, raise the read timeout for that retry, and amend the plan.
- **Verifier:** confirmed. Two sub-claims were wrong: the C-2 comment *was* updated (`vertex.py:928-932`), and the `_grade_job` re-ask loop is pre-existing, so "4 calls instead of 2" holds only for mid-size batches.

##### swe-grading-11 - `action_llm_score` still grades inside the request and is callable over RPC

This public evaluator method is no longer bound to any button but is still callable by any manager through `/web/dataset/call_kw`. It calls Vertex inside the web worker and does not check `_being_graded`, so it can collide with the lane that owns the candidate.

##### swe-grading-12 - Web writers ignore `_being_graded`, and a redundant write holds a row lock across a call
**low** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Partly fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `models/assessment.py:2656-2666, 5172-5174, 2874-2881, 653-658, 4774-4781`
- **What:** "Release Results" (all and single) writes `results_released` on every submitted evaluator including ones a lane is grading, and a `subjective_threshold` change rewrites up to 500 needs_llm answers inline. Either commit can hand the lane a SerializationFailure, so paid results are rolled back and bought again next tick. Separately `_llm_score_begin` calls `_llm_score_start` again after `_auto_score_mark_scoring` already committed it; the duplicate UPDATE holds that row's lock while the lane waits on Vertex.
- **Evidence:** Odoo cursors run REPEATABLE READ (`grading_cache.py:47` explicitly downgrades its own), so a mid-lane commit does collide; `cr.commit()` clears the env cache, which is why the second write re-issues the UPDATE.
- **Impact:** Up to about 12 paid calls wasted per release/threshold click during a run; web requests stall on a row lock.
- **Fix:** Skip or refuse `_being_graded()` candidates in the release and threshold paths, and drop the second `_llm_score_start`.
- **Verifier:** confirmed on both writers and on the duplicate write.

**low** · confirmed · not reproduced · now: **Resolved in docs; code unchanged** (§7.2)

The additions are defensible (`prompts/scoring.md:39` instructs the model to follow `scoring_guide`; `_task`'s docstring explains Form Studio keeps the scenario in `description`), and `CHANGE_SUMMARY_for_review.md:17` already documents them - only the two plan docs disagree.
- **Impact:** The token measurements in `scoring_speed_plan.md` 5.2, and any later reviewer's read of the request, are both slightly wrong.
- **Fix:** Amend the W12 bullet and `scoring_speed_plan` 5.2 to name the three fields, or drop them if the owner meant the list literally.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### apc-6 - Reviewer docs are out of step: CHANGE_INVENTORY not updated, and the summary's Flutter test count is wrong
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Resolved in docs** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `docs/CHANGE_INVENTORY.md`; `docs/CHANGE_SUMMARY_for_review.md:4-5`
- **What:** W16's last bullet asks for both files to carry the final list for reviewers. `CHANGE_INVENTORY.md` still has its pre-build mtime (18 Sep 20:07) and describes the earlier waves only, so a reviewer using it as the inventory misses all of W1-W16. `CHANGE_SUMMARY_for_review.md` was updated but claims "Flutter 1,908 passing"; the real run is 1,906 passed and 1 skipped.
- **Evidence:** `ls -la docs/` (18 Sep vs 22 Sep 19:28); the inventory still says "50 files, +9078/-193" against today's `git diff HEAD --stat` of 96 files / +12945/-1753; two independent Flutter runs both ended "+1906 ~1: All tests passed!".
- **Impact:** A reviewer working from the inventory reviews the wrong change set, and the headline numbers do not match a real run.
- **Fix:** Update `CHANGE_INVENTORY.md` for Wave 3 and re-derive the Flutter count from the run that gates the push.
- **Verifier:** confirmed - except the Odoo figure. "2,133 passing / 0 failed" is correct (see refuted `apc-1`), so only the Flutter count and the stale inventory stand.

##### apc-8 - The new instructions fingerprint that ops must check after deploy is written down nowhere
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Resolved in docs** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `docs/final_implementation_plan.md:424`
- **What:** §6 gives ops a post-deploy check whose expected value is never stated. The old value is named four times (`bundled:34c42d2f`, plus the fallback `bundled:b39fc051`); the new one is not.
- **Evidence:** Computed independently as `sha256(prompts/scoring.md.strip())[:8]`: the current tree is `bundled:3702673a`, while HEAD and the baseline lane are both `bundled:34c42d2f`. `grep 3702673a docs/*.md` returns nothing.
- **Impact:** The check cannot be performed without running the hash by hand, and the value changes on any further edit to `prompts/scoring.md` before the push.
- **Fix:** Write the fingerprint into §6 and into the runbook's step 9, and re-derive it as the last step before the push.
- **Verifier:** confirmed by computing the hash on all three trees.

##### apc-12 - The engineer cache switch is named in only one of the four documents ops will read
**low** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Resolved in docs** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `docs/final_implementation_plan.md:418-419`; `docs/calibration_runbook.md:225-228`
- **What:** Both places tell the engineer to turn the switch on ("On only if calibration passed"; "Turn the engineer switch to 'Question groups' on calib_new first") without naming the system parameter or its value. The switch is deliberately absent from every UI, so the name is the only way to set it.
- **Evidence:** `services/scoring.py:1440` `_CACHE_SWITCH = "assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache"`, compared against the literal `"groups"` at `:1467`, default `off` (confirmed at runtime). `grep scoring_cache docs/*.md` (excluding the knowledge base) matches only `CHANGE_SUMMARY_for_review.md:18`.
- **Impact:** The engineer cannot carry out the step the plan and the runbook both ask for without reading a third document.
- **Fix:** Put `assessments_be_v2.scoring_cache = groups` in §6 and in runbook step 6.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

##### pm-ux-admin-23 - The bank import dialog's footer carries five buttons, three of them downloads
**enhancement** · confirmed · **reproduced** · now: **Fixed (fix round)** (§7.2)
- **Where:** `views/bank_import_views.xml:50-70`
- **What:** The footer reads "Import as drafts | Download Template | JSON Template (Harness) | JSON Template (Native) | Cancel". Three template downloads sit at the same level as the one action the dialog exists for, and the two JSON ones encode a format distinction the dialog's own body says is detected from the file.
- **Evidence:** Dumped the live modal.
- **Impact:** The primary action does not dominate, and the footer asks the admin to understand two JSON dialects before picking a download.
- **Fix:** Collapse the three downloads into one "Download a template" dropdown and leave Import and Cancel in the footer.
- **Verifier:** confirmed.

## Part 8 - Production validation round 1 register (2026-09-23)

### 8.1 Scope, method and safety

Everything in this wave was checked against **live production** (https://projects.ethara.ai, https://assessment.ethara.ai), read-only, signed in as admin and as a real candidate. Production runs the committed code: `assessments_be_v2` 19.0.3.22.0 = git HEAD; the deployed app = FE HEAD `48e8434`. Our work is the staged backend diff (19.0.3.23.0) and the uncommitted Flutter tree. Our Flutter build was also served locally, pointed at the prod API, so old and new UI were compared on the same real records.

**Method.** 10 domain investigators (4 Flutter, 6 backend/Odoo) plus 1 real-candidate session. Then 17 skeptic agents re-checked every WRONG / PARTLY / MISSED / UNVERIFIABLE verdict and every high-severity RIGHT one: 140 checked, 17 overturned. The validation lead re-checked the blockers (now Part 1 §1.4.1) by hand.

**Safety.** Every prod call went through an allowlist guard (`ro.py`, `browser.py`; session scratch files, not in the repo). Only read routes and read methods got through; Odoo buttons, saves and API writes were aborted. Guard refusals: 3x `ir.http/lazy_session_info`, and 1x `web_save` fired by **prod's own LLM Budget page when opened** (the deployed Odoo screen writes a transient record just by being viewed). No re-score, release, kill, launch, import or exam start was sent. Two side effects: one agent's first query mis-filtered and pulled another applicant's answer snippets into its own output (read-only, discarded); opening the Emails tab in the deployed app fired that build's own per-candidate fan-out once (up to 711 reads).
